bestFor.text: THE ONE PRODUCT IN THIS RANGE THAT SITS COMFORTABLY INSIDE THE NEW AUXILIARY-DWELLING ROUTE. At a verified 33.00 m2 it clears the 32 m2 floor of the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling provision introduced by S.I. 338 of 2026 and sits 12 m2 under its 45 m2 ceiling — the only model here with headroom at both ends. THAT ROUTE REQUIRES the unit to be to the REAR of the house, to have services LINKED to the main dwelling, and 14 DAYS' NOTICE to the planning authority; it also EXPIRES ON 31 DECEMBER 2030. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on floor area this is the natural choice — but the conditions, not just the size, decide whether it qualifies.

THE LARGEST UNIT THE CLASS 3A ROUTE PERMITS — AND IT SITS EXACTLY ON THE LIMIT. At a verified 45.00 m2 it meets the ceiling of the Detached Auxiliary Dwelling provision precisely, with ZERO HEADROOM: 45 m2 qualifies, 45.5 m2 does not. FOR A COUPLE, OR A PARENT WHO NEEDS A SPARE ROOM, this is the most space obtainable without a full planning application, and the flexible one-or-two-bedroom layout is what makes 45 m2 worth having. THE CONDITIONS STILL APPLY: rear siting, linked services, 14 days' notice, and expiry on 31 December 2030. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: excellent size, no tolerance — the as-built figure must be confirmed in writing.

A GENUINE TWO-BEDROOM HOME IN THE GARDEN — AND THE ONE PRODUCT HERE THAT REQUIRES FULL PLANNING PERMISSION ON AREA. At a verified 48.00 m2 it EXCEEDS the 45 m2 Class 3A ceiling by 3 m2, so the fast auxiliary-dwelling route is unavailable regardless of siting or services; and as a habitable dwelling it was never eligible for the 30 m2 incidental exemption. FOR A FAMILY WHOSE REQUIREMENT IS ACTUALLY TWO BEDROOMS, that may be the right trade: apply properly, and build the size the household needs. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the largest unit is the one with the longest timeline — plan for a full application from the outset.

THE SAME WELLNESS BUYER AS THE QUU, AND ATLAS CANNOT SEPARATE THE TWO MODELS. Neither the Aurea nor the Quu publishes an internal floor area, an external footprint, a height, a heater specification, a warranty or a price, so nothing in the record tells a homeowner which is larger, hotter, better built or dearer. CATALOGUE LIMITATION recorded once for this supplier: with two identically documented models, no evidence-based distinction can be drawn between them, and none has been invented. WHAT CAN BE SAID applies to both: a purpose-built outdoor sauna cabin, held under Garden Rooms only because Atlas has no correct category, whose footprint nonetheless counts toward the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the choice between Aurea and Quu has to be made from the supplier's own material, not from this catalogue — ask what differs, in writing.

A HOME SAUNA BUYER — AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT PURCHASE FROM A GARDEN ROOM. Auroom supplies wellness and sauna cabins, and the certified AM-001 layer records a standing category flag: these products sit under Garden Rooms in Atlas only because no correct Product Category exists, and they should not be compared like-for-like against work-use garden rooms. THE USEFUL FRAMING is therefore not 'is this a good office' but 'is this a good sauna, and what does putting one in the garden cost you'. WHAT IS NOT HELD: no internal floor area, no footprint, no height, no insulation value, no warranty and no price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you want a sauna, judge it as one — heater type, bench layout, timber, ventilation — and then ask for the external footprint, because it counts against the same planning allowance as a garden office would.

CANNOT BE DETERMINED — THE RECORD IDENTIFIES A PRODUCT TYPE, NOT A PRODUCT. 'Ballyfree Garden Sheds — Garden Room' carries no model name, no size, no specification and no price in Atlas, and the certified AM-001 and AM-006 layers both record that no floor area, dimensions or height are published, with nothing estimated. A record at this level of generality cannot be matched to a homeowner's requirement, because there is no requirement it can be tested against. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a supplier-level entry rather than a buyable product. If Ballyfree is on your list, contact them for their actual model range and sizes, then compare those against the specified products in this catalogue — do not treat this single record as representing what the company can build.

THE ONE PRODUCT IN THIS RANGE WHOSE NAME DOES NOT ANNOUNCE A HABITABLE USE — AND THAT IS ITS ADVANTAGE. Where the Lodge and the Shepherds Hut are both marketed for overnight occupation, and therefore fall outside the Class 3 exemption on use at any size, the Beehive carries no such designation, so for a day-space use the question returns to floor area and height. NEITHER CAN BE TESTED: Atlas holds no verified floor area, and no height is published. THE JURISDICTION QUESTION STILL COMES FIRST — Berko is based in Dungiven, Co. Derry, Northern Ireland, where the Irish regime does not apply. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most promising of the three for an exempt garden room, and still unproven on figures.

OVERNIGHT ACCOMMODATION — WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT IS NOT A GARDEN ROOM DECISION. The certified record is direct: a LODGE marketed for overnight use fails the no-habitation condition, so on a Republic of Ireland site it falls outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption at any floor area. THE CLASS 3A AUXILIARY-DWELLING ROUTE may apply instead — 32–45 m2, rear siting, linked services, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030 — but Atlas holds no verified floor area, so it cannot be tested. AND THE JURISDICTION QUESTION COMES FIRST: Berko is based in Dungiven, Co. Derry, NORTHERN IRELAND, where the Irish regime does not apply at all. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle which jurisdiction governs your site before anything else.

A SMALL SLEEPING HUT WITH TRADITIONAL CHARACTER — AND THE SAME USE PROBLEM AS THE LODGE, AT A SMALLER SIZE. The certified record states it plainly: a shepherd's hut USED FOR SLEEPING fails the no-habitation condition, so on a Republic site the Class 3 exemption is unavailable however small the hut is. THAT IS THE COUNTER-INTUITIVE PART — people assume a small building is automatically safe, and on use it is not. IF IT IS USED AS A DAY SPACE ONLY — a reading room, a hideaway, a garden studio — the use condition is satisfied and the question returns to area, which Atlas cannot test because no verified floor area exists. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the answer depends entirely on whether anyone sleeps in it.

A HOMEOWNER WHOSE GARDEN, NOT THEIR WISH LIST, IS SETTING THE SIZE. This record is bespoke by definition: the certified AM-001 layer states that a measurement can exist only at as-quoted level and never at product level, so the footprint is chosen rather than given. THAT IS PRECISELY THE ADVANTAGE ON A CONSTRAINED PLOT. The certified AM-006 layer makes the practical method explicit: measure every existing shed, garage and greenhouse, subtract the total from the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, and hand the designer the remainder as an external footprint budget. Done that way, the planning outcome is decided by the buyer at the outset instead of discovered afterwards. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: best for someone willing to lead with a number rather than a picture — and to insist that the number is the EXTERNAL footprint.

Best for a therapist, practitioner or consultant with crane access who needs a CLIENT-FACING room to a consistent professional standard — and who has taken advice on change of use first. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on SIPS structural insulated panels with highly insulated ECOTHERM rigid board in all walls, roof and ceiling, and A-rated low-E high-security windows and doors, double glazed with triple glazing available. Installation is TURNKEY: factory-built at Bandon, Co. Cork, CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER, then delivered and installed. Published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE. The certified installation record makes the commercial point directly: for a treatment room the factory-finish route matters, because a client-facing space needs a CONSISTENT STANDARD OF FINISH and an engineer-certified factory build delivers that more reliably than an on-site assembly. THE QUALIFIER: a treatment room implies clients visiting the property, which raises a CHANGE-OF-USE question distinct from the area test. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: excellent shell, unresolved consent — and a heating specification you must establish separately.

Best for a buyer who has already accepted that this is a CONSENT QUESTION BEFORE IT IS A PRODUCT QUESTION — and the certified planning layer is unambiguous about why. A unit fitted with BOTH a bathroom AND a kitchenette is equipped for habitation, and the Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires incidental use with NO HUMAN HABITATION. Regardless of its area, this product is UNLIKELY TO QUALIFY as an exempt garden structure. The applicable route would be CLASS 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling — 32 to 45 m2, to the rear, linked to the services of the principal house, 14 days' notice to the planning authority, EXPIRING 31 DECEMBER 2030 — which has a 32 m2 FLOOR, so a smaller unit falls between the two routes and needs full permission. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: SIPS with EcoTherm PIR in all walls, roof and ceiling; A-rated low-E glazing, triple available; factory-built, ENGINEER-CERTIFIED, craned and installed; 20-year guarantee. Press-reported: a 25 m2 unit with bathroom and kitchenette at EUR 60,000-70,000. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: take planning advice before ordering.

Best for an Irish homeowner with crane access who wants a workspace AND integral storage in one factory-built, engineer-certified unit, and who cares more about how the building is made than about a published square-metre figure. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on SIPS — structural insulated panels 'manufactured by Europe's leading SIPS manufacturer' — with highly insulated ECOTHERM rigid board in all walls, roof and ceiling, and A-rated low-E high-security windows and doors as standard, double glazed with TRIPLE GLAZING AVAILABLE on request, in PVC, aluminium or aluclad. Installation is TURNKEY: built in full at the supplier's premises in Bandon, Co. Cork, CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER, and only then delivered and installed. Published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE. Custom-built over a press-reported six-to-eight-week period. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the construction system and the build process are the strongest in the catalogue; the missing number is the footprint, and with integral storage you need the TOTAL, not the office alone.

Best for an Irish homeowner with crane access who wants an undivided, high-specification garden building whose use can change over time — office now, studio or hobby room later — and who values construction quality over a published area. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on SIPS structural insulated panels from a named European manufacturer, with highly insulated ECOTHERM rigid board in all walls, roof and ceiling, and A-rated low-E high-security windows and doors as standard, double glazed with triple glazing on request. Installation is TURNKEY: built in full at the supplier's Bandon, Co. Cork premises, CERTIFIED BY THE SUPPLIER'S OWN ENGINEER, then delivered and installed. Published 20-YEAR GUARANTEE. Custom-built. THE QUALIFIER, from the certified AM-006 record: 'MULTI USE' DESCRIBES FLEXIBILITY, NOT A SIZE, and it raises the use condition — the 30 m2 exemption holds only while the building stays INCIDENTAL to the house and is NOT SLEPT IN. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in writing, and be specific about which of the multiple uses you actually intend.

THE ONE LASITA MAJA RECORD WITH NO SPECIFICATION AT ALL, AND THE ONLY ONE OF THE TEN THAT CANNOT BE ASSESSED. The manufacturer's product page returned METADATA ONLY, with no specification table, on two separate attempts at two separate paths, while every other Lasita page in this range returned a full table on the first attempt — so the model may be withdrawn or the page may be broken. NO AREA HAS BEEN RECORDED AND NOTHING HAS BEEN ESTIMATED, so neither the 30 m2 combined allowance nor the height limits can be tested. WHAT APPLIES IS THE SUPPLIER POSITION: solid Nordic spruce log, DIY kit only, base excluded, Republic of Ireland unconfirmed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: establish whether this model is still sold before spending any time on it.

A LARGE GABLE-ROOFED TIMBER ROOM WITH A VERIFIED 19.11 m2 INTERNAL FLOOR — the enclosed base of 21.73 m2 corroborates it exactly against the stated 44 mm logs. ON PLANNING THE FIGURE THAT COUNTS IS THE MARKETED ENVELOPE OF 5.6 × 4.4 m, i.e. 24.64 m2 INCLUDING ROOF OVERHANG, which is inside the 30 m2 combined allowance but leaves only about 5 m2 for everything else. THE HEIGHT TEST DEPENDS ON A CHOICE THE BUYER MAKES: this is a GABLE roof, so the 4 m limit applies ONLY IF IT IS TILED OR SLATED — and the standard specification ships with NO ROOF COVERING AT ALL. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the roof covering you choose decides which height test applies to your building.

Best for a homeowner whose requirement does not fit a catalogue — an awkward plot, a mixed use, an unusual shape, a specific internal height — and who would rather design the building than choose one. The supplier publishes it exactly that way: 'Have a unique vision? We design and build fully bespoke garden rooms tailored to your exact needs, style, and space — delivering a one-of-a-kind solution that works perfectly for you.' The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with on-site construction in 2–5 days and NO CRANE REQUIRED, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND on the strongest cross-border evidence in this Atlas. THE STRUCTURAL ADVANTAGE: because you set the footprint, YOU CONTROL THE PLANNING OUTCOME — the building can be designed deliberately inside the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m / 4 m height limits rather than accepted at whatever a fixed model happens to be. THE OPEN ITEMS: nothing is published on area, price, insulation specification or the base, and the warranty duration is contested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this route rewards a prepared buyer and offers nothing to an unprepared one.

Best for a family in the north-east or the Dublin corridor who needs more room to live and has decided against a house extension. The supplier's own framing is the honest one: 'create valuable additional room without the cost and disruption of a full extension'. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on a range explicitly designed for year-round use, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with the building constructed ON SITE from start to finish in 2–5 days and NO CRANE REQUIRED, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND on the strongest cross-border evidence in this Atlas — an Irish phone line, Irish location pages and euro pricing. Payment is staged at 10 per cent to book, 50 per cent on day one and 40 per cent on completion, with finance available. THE TWO OPEN ITEMS: no area is published because the build is bespoke, and the warranty duration is contested between ten years and ten months. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a genuinely usable extra room delivered in under a week — with the footprint and the warranty term both for you to settle in writing.

Best for a home trainer in the north-east or Dublin corridor whose garden cannot take a craned unit and who wants the room sized around the equipment rather than the equipment squeezed into a catalogue size. The supplier publishes the gyms as 'built to handle equipment, reduce noise, and provide a motivating environment all year round'. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with on-site construction in 2–5 days and NO CRANE REQUIRED, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND on strong published cross-border evidence. THE BESPOKE ROUTE IS A GENUINE ADVANTAGE FOR THIS USE: a gym is the one garden building where internal clear height is decisive, and a buyer specifying the design can size for it — something no fixed-model supplier permits. THE OPEN ITEMS ARE SIGNIFICANT: no internal height, no floor specification, no acoustic specification and no base position are published, and the warranty duration is contested between ten years and ten months. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bring an equipment list to the design meeting and get every one of those onto the drawing.

Best for a remote or hybrid worker in the north-east or the Dublin corridor whose plot cannot take a craned unit. The certified installation layer records the building as constructed ON SITE from start to finish in 2–5 days with NO CRANE ACCESS REQUIRED — which is the deciding fact on a terraced or side-access-only garden, where factory-built pods from Big Man Tiny Homes or ÖÖD are physically impossible. The certified thermal layer establishes YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on a range published as 'warm in winter and cool in summer, and specifically designed for year-round use', which is what an office used five days a week through an Irish winter actually requires. AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND with dedicated Dublin and Swords location pages. Payment staged 10 / 50 / 40 per cent with finance available. THE OPEN ITEMS: no area published, because you specify it; warranty duration contested between ten years and ten months. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the lowest-access-risk office route in this Atlas — settle the footprint and the warranty in writing.

Best for a beauty, hair, therapy or creative practitioner moving out of rented premises and into their own garden — and who has taken planning advice on change of use before approaching the supplier. The product is published explicitly for this: 'Run your business from a professional, dedicated space at home. Ideal for beauty, hair, therapy, or creative studios', offering 'privacy, comfort, and a welcoming environment for clients'. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED on site in 2–5 days with no crane required, a published builder's-finish standard, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND. THE COMMERCIAL ADVANTAGE IS THE BUILD WINDOW: two to five days means a practice loses almost no trading time. THE DECISIVE QUALIFIER: clients visiting the property is NOT incidental use, so the 30 m2 back-garden exemption is not a safe assumption — this is a consent question before it is a product question. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: settle the planning position first, then the plumbing, then the warranty.

Best for a family providing a calm, regulated space for a child or adult with sensory processing needs — and it is the only product in this Atlas published for that purpose. The supplier states it directly: 'Create a calm, safe space tailored to relaxation and sensory needs. Designed with comfort, insulation, and sound control in mind, these rooms provide a peaceful retreat for both children and adults.' The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED, TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED on site in 2–5 days with no crane required, and AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND. TWO THINGS MAKE THE BESPOKE ROUTE RIGHT FOR THIS USE: sensory requirements are individual, so a room designed around the specific need beats any fixed model; and the short build window limits the disruption — noise and strangers in the garden — that is itself difficult for the person the room is for. THE OPEN ITEM THAT MATTERS MOST: the 'sound control' the product is sold on is nowhere specified. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what sound control consists of in construction terms before ordering.

CANNOT BE MATCHED TO A HOMEOWNER — THE RECORD IS A RANGE, NOT A BUILDING. The certified AM-001 layer classifies it as range-level with no area, no dimensions and no product URL, and states it must be split into its constituent models before any measurement can attach. A range name tells a buyer nothing about how big the room is, how tall it stands or what it costs, so there is no requirement it can be tested against and no recommendation that can honestly be made. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED DELIBERATELY: it would be easy to present 'CUBE' as the squarer or more contemporary option against the supplier's other records, and nothing supports that. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask the supplier which models make up the CUBE range and for the external footprint and height of each, then compare those against the catalogue.

Best for a UK homeowner who wants a year-round home gym without giving over most of the garden to it. At 12 m2 published as 4 m x 3 m this is the smallest of the three Cabin Master gyms and the one that leaves the most of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance intact for anything else on the plot. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single named-manufacturer specification — silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm, double-glazed uPVC, EPDM or Kerbit SBS roofing, damp-resistant FSC MDF lining — and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations, internal electrics, flooring and painting inside scope over two to four days. For gym use the damp-resistant lining is the relevant detail: exercise puts significant moisture into a small sealed room. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: full specification at the most garden-efficient size in the gym range.

Best for a homeowner who wants a genuinely winter-usable home gym built and based by one contractor, and who is buying in the United Kingdom. The certified layers establish 15 m2 published as 5 m x 3 m, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single Cabin Master specification (named silver-backed rigid foam from Celotex, Kingspan or Extratherm; double-glazed uPVC; EPDM or Kerbit SBS roof; FSC MDF lining with a damp-resistant coating), and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations, internal electrics, flooring and painting inside the supplier's scope over a two-to-four-day site window. For gym use the damp-resistant lining is the specification detail that matters: exercise puts heavy moisture load into a small sealed room. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: the certified AM-005 layer records UK ONLY with no published Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: strong on envelope and on single-contractor accountability including the base; the whole proposition depends on being able to buy it where you live.

Best for a UK homeowner who wants the largest building in the Cabin Master range and intends to train in it year round — a full rack, a treadmill and floor space, rather than a corner of a shed. The certified layers establish 18 m2 published as 6 m x 3 m, the largest product Cabin Master offers in this Atlas set, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single named-manufacturer specification with double-glazed uPVC and a damp-resistant FSC MDF lining, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED covering design, delivery, foundations, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting within the same two-to-four-day window as the smaller units. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY, no published Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the base is inside the price on the model where the base matters most — 18 m2 of floor carrying dynamic load from dropped weights and machines.

Best for a UK homeowner whose garden will not take anything larger, and who needs exactly one wired desk. At 5 m2 published as 2.5 m x 2 m this is the smallest product in the Cabin Master range and one of the smallest in the entire Atlas, listed from GBP 14,400 with base, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting included. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the named-manufacturer rigid foam specification with double-glazed uPVC and a damp-resistant FSC MDF lining, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations inside scope over two to four days. Electrics are itemised: double sockets, lighting and an ethernet point, with the armoured-cable connection to the house mains requiring a separately arranged electrician. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a full-specification building at a minimum footprint — buy it for the site constraint, not for the value per square metre.

Best for a UK homeowner with a small garden who needs one properly wired desk plus storage, and wants it warm in winter. This is the largest of the three Cabin Master micro offices at 7.36 m2 published as 3.2 m x 2.3 m, listed from GBP 15,550 with base, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting included. The certified layers establish YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the named-manufacturer rigid foam specification with double-glazed uPVC, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED with foundations inside scope over two to four days. Electrics are itemised as double sockets, lighting and a dedicated ethernet point — wired connectivity at this size is unusual enough to be a real differentiator for remote work. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY, no published Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a complete, winter-capable one-person office where the price already carries the groundworks most competitors exclude.

Homeowners with a small garden who need one properly wired desk space and nothing more. At roughly 6m2 this is a true micro office, and the ethernet point signals it was designed for working rather than storage.

Best for a UK photographer or maker who wants a controlled, year-round workspace in the garden with the base and the wiring inside one contract. The certified layers establish 15 m2 published as 5 m x 3 m, YEAR-ROUND INSULATED on the single Cabin Master specification, and TURNKEY INSTALLATION INCLUDED covering design, delivery, foundations, build, insulation, internal electrics, flooring and painting over two to four days on site. Photography studios are one of the supplier's stated bespoke use cases. THE MATERIAL LIMITATION FOR THIS USE: studio work makes INTERNAL CLEAR HEIGHT and USABLE WALL LENGTH decision-critical — backdrop drop, lighting stands, working distance — and NEITHER IS PUBLISHED. The certified layers hold two dimensions only. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: UK ONLY. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the envelope suits the use; the two measurements that would confirm it works must be obtained from the supplier before committing.

A COMPACT COMBINED ROOM, STORE AND TERRACE WITH A SUPPLIER-STATED 8.35 m2 INDOOR AREA — a genuine internal figure, not a nominal size, so the usable space is known. ON PLANNING IT SITS INSIDE the 30 m2 combined allowance on any reading. BUT THE EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT IS NOT RELIABLE: the same page presents THREE MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT ENVELOPE FIGURES — a title saying 5.4 m × 2.5 m (13.5 m2), a technical field saying 470 × 220 cm (10.34 m2), and a marketing badge saying '8 m2 + 3 m2 terrace', which also disagrees with the technical terrace figure of 2.52 m2. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the internal area is trustworthy; the footprint is not, and a homeowner close to the limit must obtain a confirmed external figure.

A TWO-ROOM TIMBER BUILDING WITH A SEPARATE TOOL STORE — the layout is what distinguishes it. The published 15.96 m2 internal floor is SPLIT across a main room and a smaller separate room with its own entrance, which the manufacturer suggests using for garden tools, so THE USABLE SINGLE SPACE IS SMALLER THAN THE HEADLINE FIGURE by an amount not published. ON AREA IT IS EXEMPT: 16.42 m2 external against a 30 m2 combined allowance, though that is more than half of it. THE ROOF IS SHINGLED, NOT TILED, so the 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m — the 262.2 cm ridge clears it. INTENDED USE IS LISTED AS 'STORAGE'. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the room-by-room split before assuming the 15.96 m2 is one space.

Honestly, very few homeowners — and Atlas should say so. This is the smallest Concept Modular cabin at 17m², yet at EUR 32,950 it costs nearly EUR 2,000 MORE than the larger 19m² Studio in the same range. It only makes sense where the site physically cannot take a larger footprint.

A 19.1m² studio cabin for a homeowner who wants a delivered, factory-finished Irish steel-framed building with a 50-year structural warranty — and who has noticed it costs nearly EUR 2,000 LESS than the smaller 17m² cabin in the same range.

Hard to recommend over its siblings on the evidence Atlas currently holds. At EUR 49,750 for 25m² it costs EUR 11,250 more than the 26m² Studio, which is larger. Only right for a homeowner who has confirmed with the supplier that its specification materially differs.

The value pick of the Concept Modular range. 26m² at EUR 38,500 works out around EUR 1,481 per m² — the lowest of the eight Concept Modular products in Atlas, and EUR 11,250 cheaper than the smaller 25m² cabin. Best for a homeowner who wants a large, delivered, factory-finished Irish steel cabin.

The most expensive product per square metre in the Concept Modular range at roughly EUR 2,234/m². On the evidence Atlas holds today, it is only the right choice for a homeowner who has confirmed exactly what the Signature specification adds and decided it is worth the premium.

Self-contained garden accommodation, delivered factory-finished with a designer kitchen and bathroom already fitted. At 36.2m² with plumbed water and a 50-year structural warranty, this is the Concept Modular product that genuinely functions as an annexe rather than a room.

A homeowner who wants Concept Modular's steel-framed build and 50-year structural warranty in the uprated Signature specification, and is willing to pay about EUR 2,000 over the Standard Office to get it.

The entry point into Concept Modular's steel-framed range, and the cheapest route in Atlas to a 50-year structural warranty. Best for a homeowner who wants a factory-finished Irish-supplied office and values structural longevity over the lowest headline price.

A HOME OFFICE IN BERTILO'S CONCEPT FORM — A LINE NAMED FOR AN IDEA RATHER THAN A SHAPE. Unlike Cubo, Cubus and Pentus, the Concept name signals nothing about geometry or roof form, so not even the height test can be settled from it: no roof type, no area, no dimensions and no height are held. OFFICE USE IS AT LEAST UNAMBIGUOUS, being incidental to the enjoyment of the house and therefore permitted at any size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask first what the Concept form actually is — the roof answer changes whether your limit is 3 m or 4 m.

THE SECOND OF TWO 'ALU' RECORDS — A CONTEMPORARY GARDEN HOUSE RATHER THAN AN OFFICE, WITH THE SAME UNDESCRIBED MATERIAL DESIGNATION. 'ALU' points at aluminium in the cladding or joinery, but no specification confirms what it covers on this product and none has been inferred. AS A GENERAL GARDEN HOUSE RATHER THAN A CONFIGURED OFFICE, its use is whatever the household makes of it — which keeps it inside incidental use so long as nobody sleeps in it. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the material is the reason to look; the material specification is the thing to ask for.

A CONTEMPORARY GARDEN OFFICE WITH AN ALUMINIUM-RELATED DESIGNATION — ONE OF ONLY TWO 'ALU' RECORDS IN THE RANGE. 'ALU' is a materials abbreviation used across the building trade, and its appearance in a model name signals that the cladding or joinery differs from the standard timber build; NO SPECIFICATION CONFIRMS WHAT IT DENOTES HERE and none has been inferred. ON PLANNING, office use is incidental and therefore permitted, so only area and height are live — and neither is held. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the aluminium element is why you are interested, ask the supplier to describe exactly which parts it applies to.

A COMPACT OFFICE POD — THE 'POD' DESIGNATION SIGNALLING A SMALL, SELF-CONTAINED BUILDING RATHER THAN A ROOM. That is a useful distinction in a range whose risk sits at the large end: a pod is the least likely form here to trouble the 30 m2 combined allowance, though no audited area is held and nothing has been estimated. OFFICE USE IS INCIDENTAL and therefore permitted outright, so area and height are the only live tests — and neither figure is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the lowest-risk office in the range on shape, with the footprint still to confirm by SKU.

THE FOURTH AND LAST OF THE RANGE'S CONTEMPORARY ROOMS — same style designation, same absence of a size qualifier, same absence of any measurable figure. THE SAME 25 m2 FOOTPRINT AS THE 44 mm VERSION, IN QUICK-GARDEN'S HEAVIEST PLAIN LOG WALL. THE HEAVIEST-WALLED BUILDING IN THE RANGE, AND IT CARRIES THE SAME PLANNING ANSWER AS THE 44 mm VERSION: 36 m2 on the verified external footprint, which EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance outright even after the 27 July 2026 increase. A LARGE ROOM WITH A COVERED TERRACE — AND THE PLANNING POSITION IS DECISIVE AND EASILY MISREAD. AN OUTDOOR-LIVING PAVILION WITH A LARGE COVERED AREA — AND THE CLEAREST EXAMPLE IN THE CATALOGUE OF WHY INTERNAL AREA MUST NEVER BE USED FOR THE PLANNING TEST. A LONG, NARROW ROOM WITH NOTHING TO COMPLICATE THE AREA TEST — 5.5 × 2.5 m is 13.75 m2 against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving over 16 m2 for anything else, and there is no canopy or terrace to argue about. THE ENTRY POINT TO THE DOMINATOR RANGE — 8.75 m2 against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving over 21 m2 for anything else, so the exemption is never in question. THE 3 m HEIGHT LIMIT APPLIES because the roof is not tiled or slated pitched. THE LARGEST DOMINATOR WITH A COMFORTABLE PLANNING MARGIN — 5.5 × 3.5 m is 19.25 m2 against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving nearly 11 m2 for anything else on the plot. Homeowners who want an Irish-made, low-maintenance garden room and who are deliberately choosing between a materials-only kit and a fully finished room. The two-tier price structure makes that decision explicit rather than burying it in the small print.

Best for an east-coast Irish homeowner who wants the LARGEST room this supplier builds — a single open span for a studio, a family room or an office-plus-lounge — and whose garden has nothing else standing on it. THE SMALLEST PLANNING FOOTPRINT IN AN IRISH RANGE WHERE EVERY SIZE IS PUBLISHED. 9 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves 21 m2 for everything else in the garden — and 9 m2 also sat well inside the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026, so nothing about this product depends on the 2026 change. IT WAS COMFORTABLY INSIDE THE PRE-2026 25 m2 LIMIT TOO. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for one square metre more than the 5.0 m × 3.0 m model, this is the size at which a garden room stops being a corridor — the most consequential step in the range.

A LONGER ROOM THAT USES EXACTLY HALF THE ALLOWANCE. 15 m2 against the 30 m2 combined figure leaves 15 m2 — a clean midpoint, and enough remaining for a shed and a store without arithmetic. A FULL MULTI-PURPOSE ROOM — 20 m2 WITH 4 m OF DEPTH, WHICH IS THE COMBINATION MOST HOUSEHOLDS ACTUALLY WANT. NOT AVAILABLE TO IRISH HOMEOWNERS — OUT OF PRACTICAL REACH RATHER THAN OUT OF QUALITY. essexgardenstudios.co.uk serves South East England and Atlas holds no evidence of an Irish purchasing route, so however the product performs, an Irish buyer cannot currently obtain it. Confirm Irish availability before spending any time on this record.

Best for a golfer with a clear garden and no other outbuildings, wanting a long room that fits inside the planning exemption. At 27 m2 within a 28.37 m2 footprint, almost the whole structure is usable length for swing and ball flight.

Best for a golfer wanting slightly more width than Sim 1 while still fitting inside the planning exemption, on a clear garden with no other outbuildings. The 618 cm length gives the same swing and ball-flight distance as Sim 1.

Best for a household wanting a dedicated domestic gym or studio in the supplier's thickest wall specification, on a 420 x 520 cm plan that gives clear floor for equipment without a veranda taking ground. The middle size of the three-step Roland ladder.

Best for a household wanting a large dedicated gym or studio that still fits the planning exemption, on a square 520 x 520 cm plan giving clear floor in both directions for equipment. The largest of the three-step Roland ladder.

A PLACE-NAMED GARDEN HOUSE RATHER THAN A GEOMETRIC ONE — Baltrum is a North Sea island, and the naming suggests a traditional coastal cabin character rather than the cube and pent forms that dominate the range. NO SPECIFICATION CONFIRMS WHAT THE NAME DENOTES, and none has been inferred. THE MEASURABLE POSITION IS THE RANGE'S: no audited area, no height, so the 30 m2 combined allowance and the height limits cannot be tested, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge this one on appearance, and get every figure from the supplier.

THE BALTRUM 2 AS A PACKAGE — AND THE PACKAGE IS THE PLANNING QUESTION. 'Set' implies the house supplied with something further: a store, a canopy, a veranda or an annexe of some kind. NOTHING RECORDED CONFIRMS WHAT IT INCLUDES, and none has been inferred — but the possibility matters, because ANY ADDITIONAL ROOFED ELEMENT COUNTS TOWARD THE COMBINED 30 m2 alongside the house itself. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD FOR EITHER PART. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what is in the Set, and whether any of it is roofed — that answer changes the area you must count.

THE PLAIN VERSION OF BERTILO'S LEAST DESCRIPTIVE LINE. Where Cubo and Cubus signal a cube and Pentus a pent roof, 'Concept' signals nothing about form, geometry or roof type — and none has been inferred. THAT MATTERS BECAUSE THE ROOF FORM DECIDES THE HEIGHT TEST: 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof, 4 m only for a tiled or slated pitched one, and this record settles neither. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the record with the least in it — every question has to go to the supplier.

A CONTINENTAL GARDEN HOUSE — AND, ON CURRENT EVIDENCE, NOT AN IRISH PURCHASE. The certified layers record the two facts that govern every Bertilo product: NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD, and shipping is ESTONIA-ONLY with no Irish distributor. The 30 m2 combined allowance therefore cannot be tested, and there is no published route by which an Irish homeowner could buy this at all. THE MODEL NUMERAL IS A NAME, NOT A MEASUREMENT — recorded explicitly in the certified layers, so 'Cubo 1' says nothing about square metres and has not been read as doing so. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat this as a reference record rather than a live option unless a distributor is established.

THE SECOND CUBO — AND ATLAS CANNOT SAY WHAT THAT MEANS. The certified layers record that Bertilo model numerals are NOMINAL NAMES, NOT SQUARE METRES, so nothing about the step from Cubo 1 to Cubo 2 is established: not size, not specification, not price. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED BETWEEN THEM DELIBERATELY. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS THE SAME FOR BOTH: no audited area, no height, and Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor, so neither the 30 m2 combined test nor the height limits can be run and no Irish purchasing route exists. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you are comparing Cubo models, the supplier is the only source that can distinguish them.

A CUBO CONFIGURED FOR SITTING RATHER THAN WORKING — THOUGH WHAT 'LOUNGE' CHANGES IS NOT RECORDED. Bertilo offers Lounge variants across several of its forms, which suggests a distinct layout or opening arrangement, but Atlas holds no specification confirming what the designation denotes and none has been inferred. THE GOVERNING FACTS ARE THE RANGE'S: no audited area, no height, and Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run and no Irish purchasing route exists. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what the Lounge configuration actually alters — layout, glazing or size — because the answer may change the planning position.

THE HIGHEST-NUMBERED CUBO — AND THE NUMERAL STILL CONVEYS NO AREA. The certified layers record Bertilo numerals as nominal names rather than square metres, and that caution applies with most force at the top of a line, where a buyer is most likely to assume the number means more space and may be paying accordingly. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so neither the 30 m2 combined allowance nor the 3 m and 4 m limits can be tested. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: whatever you are told about this model's size, ask for it in metres and in writing.

THE LARGEST-NAMED LOUNGE VARIANT IN THE CUBO LINE — AND TWO UNRECORDED VARIABLES STACK ON IT. The numeral is a nominal name rather than an area, and the Lounge designation has no specification recorded against it either, so a buyer is choosing on two words that Atlas cannot define. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the Bertilo record where the fewest of a buyer's assumptions are supported — ask the supplier for the external footprint, the height and a description of what the Lounge configuration changes, in one written reply.

THE ENTRY MODEL OF BERTILO'S SECOND CUBE-NAMED LINE — AND A GOOD ILLUSTRATION OF WHY NAMES ARE NOT EVIDENCE. Bertilo runs BOTH a Cubo line and a Cubus line, and Atlas holds nothing that distinguishes them: no audited area, dimensions, height or specification for either, so what separates a Cubus 1 from a Cubo 1 is not recorded and has not been inferred. THE GOVERNING CONSTRAINTS ARE THE RANGE'S: no testable area against the 30 m2 allowance, no height, Estonia-only shipping and no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask the supplier what separates the two lines before choosing between them.

THE MID MODEL OF THE RANGE'S MOST EXTENDED FORM — the Cubus 2 also appears as an Office, a Lounge and a Poolhouse, so a buyer choosing this base version is choosing the simplest of four configurations of the same building. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED IS ANYTHING MEASURABLE: no audited floor area, no dimensions and no height are held, so the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size. AVAILABILITY IS THE PRIOR PROBLEM: Estonia-only shipping, no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: decide the configuration first, then get that specific variant's footprint in writing.

THE CUBUS 2 IN ITS LEISURE CONFIGURATION — one of four versions of the same model, and the one aimed at sitting rather than working. WHAT THE LOUNGE DESIGNATION CHANGES IS NOT RECORDED in any certified layer and has not been inferred: it may alter glazing, layout, plan depth or nothing measurable at all. THE RANGE-WIDE POSITION APPLIES UNCHANGED: no audited area, no height, Estonia-only shipping and no Irish distributor, so no statutory test can be run and no Irish route exists. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the configuration is the reason to choose this over the base Cubus 2 — so make the supplier describe it in writing.

THE TOP NUMERAL OF THE RANGE'S MOST DEVELOPED FORM — AND THE NUMERAL IS STILL A NAME. The certified layers record Bertilo numerals as nominal designations rather than square metres, so 'Cubus 3' establishes nothing about floor area, and no audited area or height is held for it. THAT MATTERS MOST AT THE TOP OF A LINE, where the building is likeliest to approach the 30 m2 combined allowance and where a buyer has the least information with which to check. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at this end of the range, a written external footprint is the entire basis of the planning decision.

THE LARGEST LEISURE CONFIGURATION BERTILO OFFERS BY NAME — top numeral, Lounge designation, in the range's most developed form. FOR A HOUSEHOLD WANTING A GENEROUS GARDEN SITTING ROOM that is the model to enquire about; it is also the record where the fewest assumptions are supported, since neither the numeral nor the Lounge designation carries a recorded meaning. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so the 30 m2 combined allowance and the 3 m and 4 m limits cannot be tested. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the footprint, the height and a description of the Lounge configuration in a single written reply.

Best for a large garden where a substantial room, a WC and integrated storage are all wanted in one structure, and where the owner is prepared to go through planning. The near-square 655 x 700 cm envelope needs an open area rather than a boundary strip.
Best for a long narrow garden or a boundary run of about 7 m, where a 12 m2 room plus an attached terrace suits summer use. The 298 cm depth keeps the structure close to a fence line.

THE ONE BERTILO LINE NAMED FOR ITS CLADDING RATHER THAN ITS SHAPE OR PLACE. 'HPL' is a materials designation used across the building trade, and its appearance in a model name signals that the exterior finish is the point of difference — but ATLAS HOLDS NO SPECIFICATION CONFIRMING WHAT IT DENOTES ON THIS PRODUCT, and it has not been read as one. THE MEASURABLE POSITION IS THE RANGE'S: no audited area, no height, no roof form, so no statutory test can be run. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the cladding is why you are interested, ask the supplier to describe it, its thickness and its expected life.

THE SECOND MODEL IN BERTILO'S CLADDING-NAMED LINE — AND THE NUMERAL SAYS NOTHING ABOUT SIZE. The certified layers record Bertilo numerals as nominal names rather than square metres, so the step from HPL 1 to HPL 2 is not quantified anywhere and has not been inferred. THE CLADDING DESIGNATION IS EQUALLY UNSPECIFIED: no panel, thickness or finish detail is held. NO AUDITED AREA, HEIGHT OR ROOF FORM, so no statutory test can be run, and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two undefined variables on one product — the size and the material both need describing in writing.

Best for a large garden where a covered outdoor room is the main objective and the 21 m2 enclosed space supports it. Suited to an owner with no other outbuildings who accepts that planning permission is likely to be needed.

THE SECOND OF BERTILO'S PLACE-NAMED HOUSES — a traditional alternative to the cube and pent forms that dominate the range. LIKE THE BALTRUM, THE NAME CARRIES CHARACTER RATHER THAN SPECIFICATION: no roof form, area, dimensions or height is recorded, and none has been inferred from the name. THE NUMERAL IS A NOMINAL DESIGNATION, not a size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR, so no purchasing route exists for an Irish buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a form worth looking at if a modern box would sit badly beside your house — with every figure and the roof covering still to be established.

A GENERAL-PURPOSE GARDEN HOUSE WITH NO SIZE, MATERIAL OR USE DESIGNATION ATTACHED — which makes it one of the more neutral records in a range full of qualifiers. No 'Large' marker, no 'ALU' suffix, no equipment sizing, no veranda: what is being bought is a plain building whose use the household decides. THE PLANNING POSITION IS THE RANGE'S: no audited area or height is held, nothing has been estimated, and the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run — though Hansa24's figures are recorded as retrievable. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a straightforward starting point; ask for the footprint by SKU.
Best for a shallow garden or boundary strip under 3 m deep where a 9 m2 room with a roofed canopy is wanted rather than an open veranda, at a lower price than the veranda version of the same model.

Best for a shallow garden or boundary strip under 3 m deep, where a 9 m2 room with an attached veranda is wanted and the 578 cm length can run along a fence. Suited to seasonal seating with a lockable room behind.
Best for a buyer who wants 16 m2 of enclosed room on a compact footprint, leaving most of the statutory allowance available for an existing or future shed. No covered outdoor space is included.

Best for a household needing a WC in the garden alongside a covered porch, built in the supplier's thickest wall specification. The narrow 339 cm width and 620 cm depth suit a run down a side boundary rather than across the end of a garden.

Best for a household that needs sanitary facilities in the garden — a poolside changing room, a guest annexe used in daylight hours, or a workshop where returning to the house is impractical. One of only four rows in the catalogue publishing a shower or WC.
Best for a shallow garden or boundary strip about 3 m deep where a 9 m2 room with a roofed canopy is wanted, and where a covered rather than open outdoor area matters for use in Irish weather.

Best for a large garden where outdoor entertaining space is the objective and the enclosed room is secondary. On published figures the porch and terrace account for 30.29 m2 of a 40.29 m2 footprint. Suited to a site with no existing outbuildings and an owner prepared to address planning.

Best for a household wanting a sheltered outdoor room with a small enclosed space behind it, built to one of the thicker wall specifications this supplier publishes. The 763 cm width suits a long boundary or the end of a garden rather than a square plot, since the depth is only 278 cm.

THE ENTRY MODEL OF BERTILO'S PENT-ROOF LINE — AND THE NAME SETTLES ONE PLANNING CONDITION. The certified layers record that a pent, or mono-pitch, roof is NOT a tiled or slated pitched roof, so the tighter 3 m height limit applies rather than the 4 m allowed for tiled pitched forms. That is knowable from the product line alone, which is more than most Bertilo records offer. EVERYTHING ELSE REMAINS OPEN: no audited area, no published height, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: you know the limit is 3 m — now get the actual height above finished ground level.

THE MID MODEL OF THE PENT-ROOF LINE, AND THE MOST CONFIGURABLE POINT IN IT — the Pentus 2 also appears as a Lounge, an Office and a Poolhouse. THE ROOF FORM SETTLES ONE CONDITION: a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so the 3 m height limit applies rather than 4 m. EVERYTHING MEASURABLE REMAINS OPEN: no audited area, no published height, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size, so the step from Pentus 1 is not quantified. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose the configuration first, then obtain that variant's footprint and high-side height in writing.

A PENT-ROOFED GARDEN SITTING ROOM — the leisure configuration of the mid Pentus model. THE ROOF FORM IS THE ONE THING THE NAME SETTLES: pent, therefore not tiled or slated pitched, therefore capped at 3 m rather than 4 m. THE LOUNGE DESIGNATION SETTLES NOTHING: no specification is recorded against it, so whether it changes glazing, layout or plan depth is unknown and has not been inferred. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the pent form suits a boundary site; everything else needs to come from the supplier in writing.

THE TOP OF THE PENT-ROOF LINE — AND THE MODEL WHERE THE 3 m CAP BITES HARDEST. A pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so 3 m applies rather than 4 m; and on a larger building the span is wider, which on a mono-pitch means the tall side rises further for the same pitch. NO HEIGHT IS PUBLISHED, so that cannot be checked, and no audited area is held either, so the 30 m2 combined test fails too. THE NUMERAL IS A NOMINAL NAME, not a size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on the largest pent model, the high-side height is the figure most likely to decide the outcome.

THE LARGEST PENT-ROOFED SITTING ROOM IN THE RANGE — the top numeral in the leisure configuration of the contemporary form. THE ROOF FORM SETTLES THE HEIGHT LIMIT AT 3 m, not 4 m, since a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched. NOTHING ELSE IS SETTLED: no audited area, no published height, a numeral that is a name rather than a size, and a Lounge designation with no recorded specification. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most attractive proposition in the range on paper, and the one with the most to confirm before it could be ordered.

Best for a household wanting all three of a 15 m2 room, covered outdoor seating and lockable storage in a single 758 cm run along a boundary, rather than separate structures scattered around the garden.

A GARDEN HOUSE WITH STORAGE ATTACHED DOWN ONE SIDE — THE TIDIEST WAY TO GET A ROOM AND A SHED ONTO ONE FOOTPRINT. A side shed shares a wall and a roofline with the main building, which uses less ground than two separate structures and looks like one object rather than two. THE PLANNING ARITHMETIC IS UNCHANGED, HOWEVER: the 30 m2 allowance is COMBINED across roofed structures, so the shed counts whether it is attached or not, and no audited area is held for either element. THE 'SUPER' PREFIX HAS NO RECORDED CONTENT and has not been read as a size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the total roofed footprint of house and shed together.

A TIMBER-FINISHED GARDEN HOUSE WITH A PENT ROOF — AND THE NAME DOES TWO USEFUL THINGS AT ONCE. 'Pent' settles the height test: a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so the tighter 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m. 'WOODLINE' SIGNALS A TIMBER TREATMENT OR PROFILE, though no specification is recorded against it and none has been inferred. IT IS ALSO THE ONE MODEL IN THE RANGE WITHOUT A NUMERAL, so there is no size ladder to misread. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD; Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two of the four planning conditions readable from the name — unusual in this range.

Best for a household wanting a substantial garden room with washing facilities but no sleeping accommodation — a poolside building, a workshop, or a studio used through the day — on a footprint that stays inside the exemption. The only Sweden fit-out whose named use does not conflict with the exemption.

A DESIGN-LED GARDEN LOUNGE — THE RANGE'S MOST OVERTLY ARCHITECTURAL LINE. 'Modern Art' is a styling claim rather than a specification, and no form, roof type, area or height is recorded against it; nothing has been inferred from the name. THE PRODUCT IS A LOUNGE BY DESIGNATION, so it is intended for sitting rather than working — which keeps it within incidental use, PROVIDED no one sleeps in it, since habitation is excluded from the exemption at any size. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: bought for appearance, and every measurable question is still open.

THE SECOND DESIGN-LED GARDEN LOUNGE — AND THE NUMERAL, AS ACROSS THE RANGE, IS A NAME RATHER THAN A SIZE. The certified layers record that explicitly, so nothing about the step from Modern Art 1 is established: not area, not specification, not price. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY BETWEEN THE TWO IS PRESERVED DELIBERATELY. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS COMMON TO BOTH: a lounge designation, therefore incidental use provided no one sleeps in it; no audited area or height, so no statutory test can be run; and Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose between the two on photographs, then ask for both sets of figures.

A ONE-PERSON DWELLING IN THE GARDEN, FOR A SOUTH EAST ENGLAND BUYER. The bedroom in the name settles the regulatory position: habitable accommodation, outside the Class 3 exemption at any area, per the certified AM-006 layer. What distinguishes this from the Studio Annexe in Atlas is only the bedroom count — no area, height or specification is published for either, so evidence neutrality is preserved and no ranking between them has been created. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose between the annexes on room count and quotation, not on anything Atlas can tell you; and confirm availability, as no Irish route is held.

A SOUTH EAST ENGLAND HOUSEHOLD NEEDING SELF-CONTAINED LIVING SPACE — not an Irish one. The certified AM-006 layer records that an ANNEXE is habitable accommodation, excluded from the Class 3 garden-structure exemption at any floor area, so this is a dwelling project rather than a garden-office purchase. The supplier serves Kent, Surrey, Sussex, Essex, Greater London, Hampshire and Berkshire only; Atlas holds no Irish route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for an Irish reader this record is catalogue completeness, not a live option. Within its own market it suits someone housing a family member and prepared for a consent process.

A TWO-PERSON HOUSEHOLD IN THE GARDEN — THE LARGEST STEP THIS SUPPLIER OFFERS, AND THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO REACH THE CLASS 3A BAND. Two bedrooms means habitable accommodation, outside the Class 3 exemption at any size. Of the three annexes it is the most likely to reach the 32 m2 Class 3A minimum, and equally the most likely to pass the 45 m2 ceiling — but the certified layers record no published area, so neither can be established. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a couple or a small family unit could live here, but the consent route depends entirely on a figure the supplier does not publish. South East England service area only.

Best for a buyer who wants the supplier's thickest wall specification on an efficient footprint, with the 14 m2 room laid out as a long 320 x 520 cm space suited to a desk run along one wall. The smallest of the three-step Roland ladder.

A STRAIGHTFORWARD GARDEN OFFICE, AND THE ONE RECORD IN THE RANGE WHOSE NAME CARRIES A NUMERAL. Whether that numeral denotes a size or a variant is not recorded, and it has not been read as either — the same caution the certified layers apply to designations across this catalogue. ON PLANNING, office use is incidental and therefore permitted, so only area and height remain live, and neither is held in Atlas. THE FIGURES ARE RETRIEVABLE, HOWEVER, which distinguishes Hansa24 from the genuinely undocumented suppliers here. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a conventional office, one number short of a complete answer.

Best for an Irish homeowner on a Kildare-centred footprint who wants the highest published glazing specification in the catalogue at the smallest size this supplier offers — a one or two person office, warm and quiet, installed in five working days. The certified thermal layer records it exactly as published: 'insulated walls, floors, and roofing as standard. Triple-glazed windows and doors ensure optimal thermal performance', with insulated laminate flooring, Canadian Red Cedar cladding, powder-coated steel roofing, hidden guttering, eco-grade frames and galvanised steel foundations, on Structural Insulated Panel construction. The supplier's own FAQ states the cost includes INSTALLATION AND ASSEMBLY, ELECTRICAL FITTINGS, INTERIOR PAINTING and insulation to walls, roofs and floors. Listed at EUR 19,950. Planning: 12.5 m2 sits comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with roughly 17.5 m2 of headroom. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a delivered price, not a kit price — and the only genuine triple-glazed standard recorded in this Atlas.

Best for an Irish homeowner on a Kildare-centred footprint who wants a proper working room — desk, storage and a second chair — with triple glazing as standard, and who does not want to spend most of the planning allowance getting it. This is arguably the best-balanced model in the range. The certified thermal layer records the shared specification: insulated walls, floors and roofing as standard; TRIPLE-GLAZED windows and doors; insulated laminate flooring; Canadian Red Cedar cladding; powder-coated steel roofing with a 50-year roof guarantee; galvanised steel foundations — with installation and assembly, electrical fittings, interior painting and insulation all inside the price. Listed at EUR 26,400, on a FIVE-DAY ONSITE BUILD with a five-week lead time. Planning: 17.6 m2 leaves about 12.4 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance — enough for a shed, not for a garage. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the size where specification, price and planning headroom line up best in this range.

Best for an Irish homeowner on a Kildare-centred footprint with an otherwise EMPTY back garden who wants a large, triple-glazed, fully installed room — a studio, a treatment room, an office with a meeting area. The certified thermal layer records the shared specification: insulated walls, floors and roofing as standard; TRIPLE-GLAZED windows and doors; insulated laminate flooring; Canadian Red Cedar cladding; powder-coated steel roofing with a 50-year roof guarantee; galvanised steel foundations; installation, electrical fittings and interior painting included. Structural Insulated Panel construction. Listed at EUR 37,500. THE DECISIVE FACT, from the certified AM-006 record: 25 m2 SITS EXACTLY ON THE THRESHOLD THAT APPLIED BEFORE 27 JULY 2026. It was at the very edge of exemption three months ago and now has 5 m2 of margin — which is all that is left for every other structure on the plot. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a large, well-specified, installed room — provided the garden is otherwise clear.

Best for an Irish homeowner on a Kildare-centred footprint who wants the LARGEST room this supplier builds, on a completely clear plot, and who has confirmed the external footprint in writing before committing. The certified thermal layer records the full published specification: insulated walls, floors and roofing as standard; TRIPLE-GLAZED windows and doors; insulated laminate flooring; Canadian Red Cedar cladding; powder-coated steel roofing with a 50-year roof guarantee; HIDDEN GUTTERING; eco-grade frames; galvanised steel foundations; installation, electrical fittings and interior painting included. Structural Insulated Panel construction. Listed at EUR 43,600. THE DECISIVE FACT, from the certified AM-006 record: 26.4 m2 EXCEEDED THE 25 m2 LIMIT OUTRIGHT before 27 July 2026 and required planning permission. It is exempt on area now, with 3.6 m2 of headroom — and that headroom is uncertain, because the measurement basis is unstated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most specified room in the range, on the thinnest planning margin in the range.

A NAMED LUGARDE CONFIGURATION WITH NO SIZE INFORMATION OF ANY KIND — which is the position of twenty of the twenty-five products in this range. 'Antwerp' is a city name, not a dimension, and Atlas holds no audited area, no dimensions and no Product URL for it; nothing has been estimated. THE EXEMPTION TEST THEREFORE CANNOT BE RUN. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS THE SUPPLIER POSITION: this is a bespoke build of a modular wall system sold through independent dealers, so the size is whatever is specified on the order. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the model name tells you nothing about exemption; the dealer's quotation is the only document that will.

THE SECOND OF LUGARDE'S TWO ROUND BUILDINGS, AND THE SECOND OF ONLY TWO PRODUCTS IN THE RANGE THAT CAN BE ASSESSED ON AREA AT ALL. A 300 cm diameter footprint is COMFORTABLY INSIDE the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance on any reading — no area is recorded because the plan shape is not published and a 3 m diameter yields roughly 6.4 to 7.5 m2 depending on whether it is circular or octagonal. NOTHING PUBLISHED DISTINGUISHES THE ARRAN FROM THE HELENSBURGH, and evidence neutrality between them is preserved. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: area is settled; height and internal usability are the questions.

Best for a buyer whose priority is enclosed floor area per euro and per square metre of garden, with no interest in covered outdoor space. The square 393 x 393 cm plan suits a corner or a compact plot.

A BESPOKE LOG BUILDING WITH NO PUBLISHED SPECIFICATION IN ATLAS — no dimensions, no area, no Product URL, nothing estimated — so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested and the record holds the verification classification. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THE USE POSITION: whatever size is ordered, exempted development requires INCIDENTAL USE and permits NO HUMAN HABITATION, so an office, gym, studio or hobby room is fine and overnight accommodation is not, at any size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the intention is guest or family accommodation, this route does not deliver it — the separate Class 3A auxiliary-dwelling route does.

THE PLAIN BARBADOS — A STRAIGHTFORWARD GARDEN ROOM WITH NO ROOFED EXTRAS, AND THEREFORE THE SMALLEST CLAIM ON THE ALLOWANCE OF THE TWO BARBADOS RECORDS. The 30 m2 is COMBINED across every roofed structure, so a room without an attached store puts less into the total — the whole of the development is the room itself. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD IN ATLAS and nothing has been estimated, so the test cannot be run from the catalogue; the certified layers do record Hansa24's dimensions as retrievable, so the figure is obtainable on request. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the simpler of the two versions, and the easier to check.

THE STORAGE VERSION OF A MODEL THAT ALSO EXISTS PLAIN — AND THE 'PLUS' IS WHAT THE PLANNING TEST MEASURES. Hansa24 offers the Barbados both with and without an integrated store, so the difference between the two records is precisely the additional roofed footprint that counts toward the combined 30 m2. NEITHER FIGURE IS HELD IN ATLAS, so the size of that difference cannot be stated, and nothing has been estimated. THE 'PLUS' DESIGNATION ITSELF HAS NO RECORDED CONTENT beyond the storage the name describes. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for both Barbados footprints and compare them — the gap is what the storage costs you in allowance.

ONE OF TWENTY LUGARDE MODELS WHOSE NAME CARRIES NO DIMENSION. No audited area, no dimensions, no Product URL and no estimate are held for the Bruges, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested and the record holds the verification classification. WHAT CAN BE SAID WITHOUT INVENTING ANYTHING: this is a bespoke build of a Dutch log manufacturer's modular system, sold only through independent dealers, with an unconfirmed Republic of Ireland route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a supplier-level decision before it is a product-level one — establish the route to Ireland first, then the size.

ANOTHER UNMEASURED LUGARDE CONFIGURATION — no dimensions, no area, no Product URL, nothing estimated — so the exemption test cannot be run and the record holds the verification classification. NOTHING HAS BEEN CHARACTERISED AS EVIDENCED ABSENCE. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat Atlas's Lugarde figures as indicative and confirm everything with the dealer.

A YEAR-ROUND INSULATED PINECA ROOM WHOSE SIZE ATLAS CANNOT ESTABLISH. The record carries the supplier's explicit INSULATED designation — insulation integrated into wall, roof and floor from the outset, materials included in the kit price — but NO SIZE OR AREA IS HELD and no Product URL, and the model did not appear on the first page of the pineca.ie garden-rooms listing when it was read. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THE THERMAL CLASS AND THE PURCHASING RULE THAT GOES WITH IT: the insulation specification must be chosen AT ORDER, because there is no retrofit path. A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION FOR WHICH NEITHER A DIMENSION NOR A PRODUCT PAGE COULD BE RETRIEVED. Atlas holds no area, no dimensions and no Product URL, and nothing has been estimated — the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION HELD IN ATLAS WITH NO MEASURABLE INFORMATION AT ALL — no dimensions, no area, no Product URL, nothing estimated.
