HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge the supplier before the model — at this level of disclosure the model name is not a decision.

Best for a large garden, most obviously one with a pool, where a 24 m2 room in the supplier's thickest wall is wanted and the owner accepts that planning permission will be needed. The 783 x 501 cm envelope needs an open area.

A SMALL ROUND GARDEN BUILDING WHOSE AREA IS EFFECTIVELY A NON-ISSUE. The name carries a 300 cm diameter — one of only two Lugarde products whose designation contains a measurement at all — and a 3 m diameter footprint is WELL INSIDE the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance whatever the exact plan shape. NO AREA FIGURE IS RECORDED, because a 3 m diameter resolves to 6.36, 7.07 or 7.46 m2 depending on whether the building is circular or octagonal and how an octagon is measured, and Atlas will not choose between them. THE LIVE CONDITION IS HEIGHT, not area: round buildings are often steeply roofed and the cap is 4 m pitched, 3 m otherwise. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the finished ridge height, not the footprint.

AS PUBLISHED, THIS CONFIGURATION IS NOT SUITED TO AN IRISH BACK GARDEN AT ALL — AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING ATLAS CAN SAY ABOUT IT. Lugarde publishes the Helsinki as 960 × 540 cm, 51.84 m2 nominal, which exceeds the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance by a wide margin AND exceeds the 32–45 m2 band of the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route — SO NEITHER EXEMPTION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS SIZE. BUT THE HELSINKI IS A CONFIGURATION, NOT A FIXED PRODUCT: it is a named example build of Lugarde's Prima modular wall system, and a buyer specifies their own size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: suited to someone who wants this design at a SMALLER ORDERED SIZE; the published example would require full permission.

THE PLAIN VERSION OF THE RANGE'S MOST DEVELOPED MODEL FAMILY — AND THE ONE WITH THE SMALLEST CLAIM ON THE ALLOWANCE. Where the veranda and shed-and-porch versions add roofed area that counts toward the combined 30 m2, this layout adds none: the enclosed room is the whole of the development. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so the test still cannot be run from the catalogue — but the certified layers record Hansa24's figures as retrievable, so the number is obtainable. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a garden where the allowance is tight, the plain layout is the version to price first.

Best for a buyer who wants a 12 m2 enclosed room with some sheltered entry, on a compact footprint that leaves most of the statutory allowance free. Suited to a small or medium garden used seasonally.

THE VERANDA VERSION OF A MODEL THAT ALSO EXISTS PLAIN AND IN A SHED-AND-PORCH LAYOUT — THREE JACOB E RECORDS, AND THE DIFFERENCES ARE ALL ROOFED AREA. That is the useful frame: within this one model family, what changes between versions is how much roofed footprint is added to the enclosed room, and the certified layers record that a roofed veranda may count toward the assessed area. NO AUDITED FIGURE IS HELD FOR ANY OF THE THREE, so the comparison cannot be made from the catalogue. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for all three Jacob E footprints together — the differences between them are exactly what the 30 m2 test measures.

A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION WITH NO AREA, NO DIMENSIONS AND NO PRODUCT URL HELD, AND NOTHING ESTIMATED — the exemption test cannot be run. THE ONE PIECE OF PRODUCT-LEVEL EVIDENCE THAT DOES APPLY EVERYWHERE IN THIS RANGE IS THE GLAZING: HR++ at U=1.1 W/m2K is published, which is a specific and verifiable figure. IT IS ALSO, NOTABLY, THE ONLY THERMAL FIGURE THE SUPPLIER PUBLISHES — there is no wall, roof or floor specification to go with it. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: good glass in an uninsulated shell is not a warm room; ask about the walls in the same breath.

THE ONLY PINECA MODELS THAT PUBLISH WHAT YOU ACTUALLY GET INSIDE. Pineca sells the LAYLA (Insulated, 34 mm + cladding) in THREE SIZES, each with its own published area: 4 × 3 m at 10 m2, 5 × 3 m at 13 m2 and 6 × 3 m at 15 m2 — and in every case the published area is MATERIALLY SMALLER than the external dimensions, by 2 to 3 m2, which is exactly consistent with an insulated build-up of log, insulation and cladding on all four sides. THAT CONFIRMS THESE FIGURES ARE INTERNAL FLOORS. ALL THREE SIT WELL INSIDE the 30 m2 combined allowance on external dimensions. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the one place in this range where the insulated wall's real cost in floor space is visible before you order.

A PLAIN NAMED GARDEN ROOM — NO SIZE MARKER, NO STYLE LABEL, NO CONFIGURATION, NO ROOFED EXTRAS. In a range of 31 products carrying qualifiers of every kind, that neutrality is itself informative: this record makes no claim the catalogue would have to qualify, and it adds nothing roofed beyond the room itself to the combined 30 m2. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD and nothing has been estimated, so the test still cannot be run — but the certified layers record Hansa24's figures as retrievable. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the simplest record in the range; one footprint to ask for and nothing else.

Best for a long boundary run of about 8 m where a household needs both a large room and lockable storage in one structure, and where almost all the ground given up is enclosed rather than covered outdoor space. The 300 cm depth keeps the building tight to a fence line.

A LUGARDE DESIGN HELD IN ATLAS WITHOUT DIMENSIONS, AREA OR A PRODUCT URL; nothing estimated, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE HONEST FRAMING FOR THIS RECORD IS THAT IT IS A DESIGN CHOICE RATHER THAN A SPECIFICATION CHOICE — the model name identifies a look, and the size, height, thermal build and price are all settled later with a dealer. FOR THE RIGHT BUYER THAT IS THE POINT, not a fault. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose it because you want this building; do not expect the catalogue to tell you whether it is exempt.

ONE OF THE RANGE'S UNMEASURED CITY MODELS: no area, no dimensions, no Product URL, nothing estimated, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE HONEST SUMMARY OF THIS SUPPLIER IS THAT ITS PRODUCTS ARE REAL AND ITS DOCUMENTATION IS NOT REACHABLE — lugarde.com is on the Atlas permanently-unreadable list, so absence here cannot even be characterised as evidenced absence. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS THE BUYING MODEL: bespoke sizing, dealer-only distribution, uninsulated as standard. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: nothing about this model can be confirmed remotely; everything comes from a dealer conversation.

ONE OF THE NINETEEN LUGARDE RECORDS HOLDING NO DIMENSIONS AT ALL — no area, no size, no Product URL, nothing estimated — so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE RANGE'S OVERALL MEASUREMENT POSITION IS RECORDED PLAINLY: NOT ONE Lugarde product is rankable on internal floor area, and three structural reasons are held for it — an unreadable manufacturer site, bespoke construction, and a split between two wall systems with no shared measurement convention. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a supplier where product comparison is not possible on published evidence, by design as much as by omission.

THE LARGEST PINECA BUILDING IN ATLAS — AND IT SITS PRECISELY ON THE LIMIT. Published as 'Garden Studio MAJA (66 mm), 7.5×4 m, 30 m2', and the stated 30 m2 is exactly 7.5 × 4 m, so the figure Pineca publishes here is the EXTERNAL FOOTPRINT. That places it EXACTLY ON the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance WITH ZERO HEADROOM: any existing shed, garage or store on the plot puts the total over, and before 27 July 2026 it exceeded the old 25 m2 threshold outright. IT IS EXEMPT ON AREA ONLY IN AN OTHERWISE COMPLETELY EMPTY BACK GARDEN. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: measure every existing structure before ordering — this is the tightest position in the Pineca range.

A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION HELD WITHOUT DIMENSIONS, AREA OR A PRODUCT URL; nothing estimated, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE POINT WORTH DRAWING OUT HERE IS THAT SIZE AND PRICE MOVE TOGETHER IN A BESPOKE RANGE: because the buyer specifies the footprint, the exemption and the budget are the same conversation rather than two separate ones. THAT IS AN UNUSUAL AND USEFUL PROPERTY, and it belongs to the supplier's model rather than to this design. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: set the maximum footprint your garden allows before asking for a price, not after.

THE SMALLEST PUBLISHED LUGARDE CONFIGURATION AND THE SAFEST ON AREA — 434 × 350 cm, 15.19 m2 nominal, which is roughly half the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance and leaves genuine room for an existing shed. IT IS ALSO THE ONE PREMIUM-SYSTEM BUILD IN ATLAS WITH A FIGURE, and the centimetre-level precision of 434 × 350 suggests a manufacturer-derived dimension rather than a rounded label — though that alone does not establish whether it is internal or external. AS A BESPOKE CONFIGURATION THE AS-ORDERED SIZE GOVERNS. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the Lugarde model least likely to create an area problem.

A LUGARDE MODEL WITH NO MEASURABLE EVIDENCE IN ATLAS — no dimensions, no area, no Product URL, nothing estimated — so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE ASSEMBLY QUESTION IS THE ONE THIS RECORD IS BEST USED TO RAISE: Lugarde publishes no installation terms, no assembly service and no installed price of its own, so whether a building arrives as a KIT or INSTALLED depends entirely on the reseller. THAT IS A LARGE DIFFERENCE IN BOTH COST AND EFFORT on a solid log building. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask the dealer in writing whether the quoted price includes assembly and base — do not assume either.

A GARDEN ROOM WITH A COVERED FRONT — A WORKING ROOM RATHER THAN A SUMMER HOUSE, WITH THE SAME VERANDA QUESTION ATTACHED. The certified layers record that a veranda may or may not count toward the assessed area depending on whether it is roofed, and that this has not been determined for the range. THE 'E' DESIGNATION IS ALSO UNRELIABLE ACROSS THE RANGE, since letters are reused between different buildings; the SKU must govern. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: quote the SKU and ask for the total roofed footprint, room plus veranda.

A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION WITH NO DIMENSIONS, NO AREA AND NO PRODUCT URL IN ATLAS; nothing estimated, so no exemption test can be run. WORTH NAMING ON THIS RECORD IS THE DELIVERY POSITION, WHICH APPLIES TO ALL 25: Lugarde's own free delivery covers the NETHERLANDS ONLY, and Irish and UK buyers are served by independent resellers — Titan Garden Buildings, ForeverTimber, Garden Chic, elbec and Simply Log Cabins are named in Atlas, but none with confirmed Irish terms. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the first question is not what size it is but whether anyone will deliver it to your address.

THE PINECA RECORD A HOMEOWNER SHOULD APPROACH MOST CAREFULLY — IT CARRIES CONFLICTING MEASUREMENTS FROM THE SUPPLIER'S OWN PAGE. Pineca publishes this model as 'Garden Room OAK (34 mm), 6×3 m, 18 m2', while the product's own URL slug reads 16 m2. THE SAME LINK STATES TWO DIFFERENT AREAS, and neither has been chosen, corrected or averaged. The arithmetic resolves nothing: 6 × 3 m is 18.00 m2 externally and 17.39 m2 internally on the published 34 mm wall — so 18 matches the external envelope and 16 MATCHES NOTHING. ON EITHER READING IT IS INSIDE the 30 m2 combined allowance, so the conflict does not change the exemption at this size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the planning answer survives the confusion; the usable-space answer does not.

THE OFFICE CONFIGURATION OF THE RANGE'S MOST DEVELOPED MODEL FAMILY — the Jacob appears plain, with a veranda, with a shed and porch, and here as an office. THAT STRUCTURE IS THE USEFUL THING: a household can pick the layout that matches its use rather than choosing between unrelated buildings. OFFICE USE IS INCIDENTAL and therefore permitted outright, so only area and height are live, and neither is held in Atlas. THE LETTER 'C' IS REUSED ACROSS DIFFERENT HANSA24 PRODUCTS, so the SKU must govern. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the cleanest layout in the family on planning — confirm the footprint by SKU.

ONE OF THE TWENTY UNMEASURED LUGARDE CONFIGURATIONS — no area, no dimensions, no Product URL, nothing estimated — so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE MATERIAL POSITION IS ESTABLISHED AND IS THE REAL BASIS FOR CHOOSING HERE: solid log board construction, offered at 28, 44 and 68 mm, from a Dutch manufacturer selling a designed range. THAT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF BUILDING FROM THE CLAD-FRAME PODS that dominate the Irish market, with different maintenance, different appearance and a different lifespan. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a material decision as much as a product one.

THE OUTLIER OF THE LUGARDE RANGE, AND THE ONE RECORD A HOMEOWNER SHOULD APPROACH WITH MOST CAUTION. 'PSML2' IS AN INTERNAL PRODUCT CODE, NOT A NAME AND NOT A MEASUREMENT: Atlas holds no dimensions or area, nothing has been estimated, and the exemption test cannot be run. A RECORD DEFECT IS ALSO HELD AGAINST IT, recorded and not corrected: its Product URL points to the DUTCH-LANGUAGE site while every other Lugarde record points to the English or UK path or holds no URL, which suggests it was captured from a different catalogue to the named city models. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm this product is offered to Irish buyers at all before going further.

ANOTHER OF THE TWENTY LUGARDE MODELS HELD IN ATLAS WITHOUT A DIMENSION — no area, no size, no Product URL, nothing estimated, so no exemption test can be run. WHAT DISTINGUISHES THIS SUPPLIER FROM OTHERS WITH THIN EVIDENCE IS THE REASON FOR IT: not that the manufacturer publishes nothing, but that its site could not be read and its products are built to order. THE PRACTICAL POSITION IS THE SAME FOR THE HOMEOWNER either way. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat every figure as outstanding, and expect to obtain them all from a dealer in one exchange rather than piecemeal.

A LUGARDE CONFIGURATION WITH NO MEASURABLE EVIDENCE IN ATLAS — no dimensions, no area, no Product URL, nothing estimated — so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE ONE CONDITION THAT CAN BE ASSESSED WITHOUT A DIMENSION IS SITING: exempted development requires the building to sit BEHIND THE FRONT WALL of the house and to leave at least 25 m2 of private open space. THAT IS A DECISION ABOUT THE GARDEN, NOT THE PRODUCT, and it applies to every model in this range equally. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: check the siting rules against your own plot first — they cost nothing to establish and can rule a garden out before any supplier is contacted.

A BESPOKE LOG GARDEN ROOM WHOSE SIZE IS DECIDED ON ORDER, NOT ON THE PAGE. Atlas holds no dimensions, no area and no Product URL for the Verona, and nothing has been estimated, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT IN THE RECORD — IT IS THE SHAPE OF THE PRODUCT: Lugarde markets these as configurations of its modular wall systems, so any figure retrieved would be an example build a buyer can vary. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: suited to someone who wants to name their own dimensions; the exemption is then designed in rather than checked afterwards.

A LUGARDE MODEL WHOSE PLANNING POSITION IS ENTIRELY OPEN. No dimensions, no area and no Product URL are held; nothing has been estimated; the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. THE HEIGHT CONDITION IS EQUALLY OPEN and worth naming: no height or roof form is recorded for any Lugarde product, and the cap is 4 m for a tiled or slated pitched roof but only 3 m otherwise — a full metre of difference on a range whose designs vary considerably in roof form. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two figures decide the exemption here, footprint and ridge height, and the dealer holds both.

A LUGARDE MODEL WITH NO PUBLISHED SIZE, HEIGHT OR AREA IN ATLAS AND NOTHING ESTIMATED — the exemption test cannot be run and the record holds the verification classification. IT IS WORTH SEPARATING TWO THINGS A HOMEOWNER MIGHT CONFUSE: the 30 m2 allowance is COMBINED ACROSS ALL GARDEN STRUCTURES, so an existing shed, greenhouse or store counts against it before this building is added. ON A GARDEN THAT IS ALREADY BUILT ON, a bespoke supplier's ability to size down is the useful feature. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: total what is already there before asking what size you can have.

THE BEST-PLACED CONFIGURATION IN THE LUGARDE RANGE ON THE EXEMPTION TEST. Published as 500 × 400 cm, 20.00 m2 nominal, it sits inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance and leaves roughly 10 m2 for every other structure on the plot — which is a real, usable margin if there is already a shed. IT IS A PRIMA SYSTEM CONFIGURATION, SO THE SIZE IS VARIABLE ON ORDER: the exemption position must be checked against the as-ordered dimensions, not this example. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the one Lugarde model where a homeowner can start the planning conversation from a figure rather than a blank.

A ROOM, A SHED AND A PORCH IN ONE BUILDING — AND ALL THREE COUNT. That is the point this record exists to make: the 30 m2 back-garden allowance is COMBINED across every roofed structure, and a product that packages a room with an attached store and a covered porch puts all of that area into a single development. A HOUSEHOLD THAT WOULD OTHERWISE BUY A ROOM AND A SHED SEPARATELY LOSES NOTHING BY COMBINING THEM — the arithmetic is the same either way, and one building is tidier. NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD FOR ANY ELEMENT. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the total roofed footprint of the whole unit.

A DEDICATED SNOOKER ROOM — AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD NAMES IT AS AMONG THE LIKELIEST PRODUCTS IN THE RANGE TO EXCEED 30 m2. The reasoning is dimensional rather than speculative: a building sized around a snooker table implies a large footprint WITH CUE CLEARANCE on every side, which is a far bigger plan than the table itself. NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD AND NOTHING HAS BEEN ESTIMATED, so the combined allowance cannot be tested. NOTE ALSO THE NAMING CAUTION: 'Hansa B' is used for at least two different buildings in this catalogue, so the SKU must govern. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in writing before ordering.

THE MIDDLE OF A DELIBERATELY SMALL RANGE — A LITTLE MORE LENGTH FOR THE SAME EASY PLANNING POSITION. The supplier designation is 10 ft × 8 ft, which the certified AM-001 layer records as 80 sq ft, or 7.43 m2 nominal on a unit conversion of the supplier's own figure. Against the 30 m2 combined allowance about 22 m2 remains for other structures, and the product was equally clear of the pre-27 July 2026 limit of 25 m2. THE EXTRA TWO FEET GO INTO LENGTH, NOT DEPTH: the room is still 8 ft front to back, so the gain is shelf and storage wall rather than a second usable zone. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose this over the 8 ft square if you need somewhere to put things as well as somewhere to sit — not if you need the room to feel bigger.

THE LARGEST HOP, AND STILL THE EASIEST PLANNING POSITION IN THE CATALOGUE. The supplier designation is 12 ft × 8 ft — 96 sq ft, or 8.92 m2 nominal on a unit conversion of the supplier's own figure. That leaves roughly 21 m2 of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance untouched, and it was equally clear of the pre-27 July 2026 limit. THE EXTRA LENGTH IS WHERE THIS MODEL EARNS ITS PLACE: at 12 ft you can put a desk at one end and a workbench, storage run or reading chair at the other, which the 8 ft square cannot do. The depth is still 8 ft, so the room remains a corridor rather than a square. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the best of this range for a single occupant who needs two zones along a wall rather than two zones across a room.

THE SMALLEST SENSIBLE STARTING POINT — A SINGLE-DESK ROOM WITH NO PLANNING QUESTION AT ALL. At a supplier designation of 8 ft × 8 ft the certified AM-001 layer records 64 sq ft, converted as a unit conversion of the supplier's own figure to 5.95 m2 nominal. Against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance that is negligible: roughly 24 m2 of allowance remains for everything else in the garden, and the product was equally clear of the old 25 m2 limit. THIS IS THE RECORD FOR A HOMEOWNER WHOSE REQUIREMENT IS MODEST AND WHOSE GARDEN IS SMALL: one desk, one chair, a door and a window. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: no realistic area exposure and no exemption arithmetic to worry about — but be honest that 8 ft square is one function only, and after wall build-up the usable interior is smaller again.

Best for a large garden where covered outdoor entertaining matters as much as the room, and where the owner is prepared to resolve the planning position before ordering. The 512 x 645 cm envelope suits an open lawn rather than a boundary run.

Best for a square area of garden or a corner, where a symmetrical 498 x 498 cm building suits the plot better than a long narrow one, and where 19 m2 in the supplier's thickest wall is wanted at the lowest published price for that combination.

A SUMMER HOUSE WITH COVERED OUTDOOR SPACE — AND THE VERANDA IS THE PLANNING QUESTION, NOT AN ACCESSORY. The certified layers record that a veranda MAY OR MAY NOT COUNT toward the assessed area depending on whether it is roofed and enclosed, and that this has not been determined for the range's veranda models. A ROOFED VERANDA WOULD BE ADDED TO THE ENCLOSED FOOTPRINT for the 30 m2 combined test. No audited area is held for either element. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask specifically whether the veranda is inside the quoted footprint — the certified layers note it can decide the exemption.

Best for a household wanting a 15 m2 room with a genuinely usable covered porch of about 8.9 m2 — large enough for outdoor seating rather than just shelter at the door. Suited to a medium garden with few other structures.
Best for a buyer who wants the largest room the exemption will accommodate without planning permission, in the supplier's thickest wall specification, on a clear garden with no other outbuildings.
Best for a shallow garden or boundary strip under 3 m deep where a small room with a roofed canopy is wanted rather than an open veranda, at the lower price of the two Nora D outdoor variants.

Best for a shallow garden or boundary strip under 3 m deep, where a small room with an attached veranda is wanted and the 578 cm length can run along a fence. Suited to seasonal seating with a lockable room behind.

Best for a household that wants a covered outdoor sitting area as the primary purpose, with a small lockable room attached. On the published figures the veranda accounts for 15.52 m2 of the 25.52 m2 footprint, so the outdoor space is the larger part of what is bought. Suited to summer and shoulder-season garden use.

Best for a clear garden with no other outbuildings, where a broad near-square 577 x 502 cm envelope can be accommodated and a 15 m2 studio room is the objective. Suited to a buyer prepared to question the supplier about the published envelope before ordering.

A ROOM BUILT AROUND A FULL-SIZE TABLE-TENNIS TABLE — AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD FLAGS THE SAME CONSEQUENCE AS THE SNOOKER MODEL: a building sized to hold the table implies a LARGER FOOTPRINT, and this use case pushes toward the limit. THE AREA HAS NOT BEEN ESTIMATED and no audited figure is held, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested from Atlas evidence. WHAT MAKES THE PRODUCT WORTH CONSIDERING is that it is designed around playing space rather than adapted afterwards. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the external footprint in m2 in writing — the certified layers record that Hansa24's dimensions are retrievable, so the figure exists.

Best for a buyer who wants enclosed floor area rather than covered outdoor space, on a site where the 30 m2 combined allowance is already partly used. Nearly all of the 12.46 m2 footprint is usable room, and the 298 cm width suits siting along a boundary.

THE ENTRY POINT OF THE COVER RANGE — AND, LIKE ITS SIBLINGS, A ROOFED STRUCTURE THAT COUNTS TOWARD THE ALLOWANCE. No floor area or dimensions are published, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run; the certified layers confirm nothing has been estimated. THE 'ESSENTIAL' NAME SIGNALS A BASE SPECIFICATION RATHER THAN A SIZE, and has not been read as either. FOR A HOUSEHOLD WHOSE REQUIREMENT IS SIMPLY SHELTER OVER A PATIO, the base edition may well be sufficient — the range's higher editions publish nothing that would prove otherwise. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the covered footprint and the height in writing and count that footprint toward the combined 30 m2.

A LOUVRED-ROOF PERGOLA — THE ONE PRODUCT TYPE HERE THAT CAN BE OPENED OR CLOSED, AND THE ONE THAT RAISES A QUESTION THE SUPPLIER DOES NOT ANSWER. Tarasola is a louvred-roof pergola line, Polish-manufactured, carried under Garden Rooms because Atlas has no correct alternative category. THE ADJUSTABLE ROOF IS THE APPEAL: shade in July, shelter in October, open sky when you want it. IT IS ALSO THE COMPLICATION — whether the roof counts as a roofed structure for the area test when the louvres are CLOSED is not addressed anywhere. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: treat a closeable louvred roof as ROOFED for planning purposes unless your local authority tells you otherwise.

A LOUVRED-ROOF PERGOLA — AND A RECORD A HOMEOWNER CANNOT TELL APART FROM ITS SIBLING. The certified layers record the issue plainly: this product and the Tarasola Technic Pro Edition are distinguished ONLY BY EDITION NAME, with no specification or size difference held in Atlas, so a homeowner cannot tell from the catalogue whether the two differ in footprint at all — AND IF THEY DO, THE PLANNING POSITION MAY DIFFER BETWEEN THEM. That is the decision-relevant consequence of an undocumented product split. No area, dimensions or height are published for either. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask the supplier to confirm in writing WHICH EDITION you are being quoted, and its covered footprint and height.

THE TOP-NAMED LOUVRED PERGOLA — AND 'PRO' HAS NOT BEEN READ AS DENOTING A LARGER UNIT. The certified layers are explicit: this product and the Tarasola Technic New Edition are separated only by edition name, with no specification or size difference held in Atlas, and no inference has been drawn from the word. NO FLOOR AREA, DIMENSIONS OR DERIVABLE FOOTPRINT are published, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run. AS ACROSS THE TARASOLA LINE, treat a closeable louvred roof as ROOFED for the area test unless your local authority says otherwise. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the covered footprint and height for the EXACT edition quoted, in writing.

THE ONE PRODUCT IN THIS SUPPLIER'S RANGE WHERE THE NAME SETTLES A PLANNING CONDITION. The certified record makes the point: a FLAT roof falls under the 3 m Class 3 height limit, NOT the 4 m limit reserved for tiled or slated pitched roofs — the tighter of the two, and knowable from the product name alone. Everything else remains open: no floor area, dimensions or derivable footprint are published, so the 30 m2 test cannot be run. IT IS A LOUVRED-ROOF PERGOLA LINE held under Garden Rooms for want of a correct category. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: you know your height limit is 3 m; get the overall height above finished ground level and check it against that.

THE ONE GARDENDREAMS RECORD SOLD AS AN ENCLOSED GARDEN ROOM RATHER THAN A TERRACE COVER — which matters, because the certified layers record that 8 of this supplier's 14 products are pergola or terrace-cover types held under Garden Rooms for want of a correct category. THE HELIOS IS NAMED AS A GARDEN ROOM AND SITS IN THE CATEGORY LEGITIMATELY. WHAT IS MISSING IS EVERYTHING MEASURABLE: no floor area, no dimensions, no height, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the height limits can be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right product type for a conventional garden-room brief, with every figure still to be obtained in writing.

COVERING A TERRACE — NOT BUILDING A ROOM, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS. The certified layers record that the GardenDreams 'Editions' are terrace-cover and pergola-type products rather than enclosed garden rooms, held under Garden Rooms because Atlas has no correct alternative category. THE PLANNING CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT: a ROOFED structure still counts toward the combined 30 m2 back-garden allowance EVEN WHEN IT IS OPEN AT THE SIDES, so a homeowner cannot treat a terrace cover as free of the area test. A TERRACE COVER FOR A GARDEN WHERE THE ALLOWANCE IS NOT YET SPOKEN FOR. Homeowners wanting a generous 16m2 room from one of the UK's largest established garden room manufacturers, where scale and trading track record matter more to them than published technical detail.

AN IRISH HOMEOWNER WHO WANTS A REAL WORKING ROOM WITHOUT GOING NEAR THE PLANNING LIMIT. A MORE TRADITIONAL LOOK AND A TALLER INTERNAL VOLUME THAN THE PENT — with a height caveat that is easily got wrong. 'Apex' denotes the roof type, not a size; the certified AM-001 layer records that explicitly. THE CAVEAT MATTERS: an apex roof qualifies for the more generous 4 m Class 3 height limit ONLY if it is tiled or slated. A pitched roof finished in felt, shingle or steel sheet falls under the 3 m limit — and a pitched roof is taller at the ridge than a pent of the same wall height, so the wrong covering makes an apex cabin MORE exposed on height, not less. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the roof covering is as important as the roof shape, and MCD publishes neither it nor the height.

THE PLANNING CONSEQUENCE IS THE THING TO UNDERSTAND, and the certified AM-006 layer states it plainly: for the 30 m2 combined allowance the WHOLE footprint counts, room and store together — the store is not free floor area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a sensible way to keep one building instead of two, provided you count the whole footprint, which MCD does not publish.

A LOW-PROFILE GARDEN ROOM WHERE HEIGHT IS THE CONSTRAINT — THE ONE THING THIS RECORD'S NAME ACTUALLY TELLS YOU. 'Pent' denotes a single-slope, non-tiled roof, which the certified AM-006 layer notes falls under the tighter 3 m Class 3 height limit but is also, in practice, the lowest roof form available: useful next to a boundary, under overlooking windows, or where a neighbour's outlook matters. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN IS EVERYTHING ELSE: no floor area, no dimensions and no height are published, so the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance cannot be tested. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the roof form is a genuine reason to shortlist; the missing footprint is the reason you cannot yet act on it.

THE SAME ROOM-PLUS-STORE IDEA AS THE APEX COMBO, IN THE LOWEST ROOF FORM. A pent roof is single-slope and non-tiled, so it takes the tighter 3 m Class 3 height limit but sits lower on the plot — which is the right choice where a boundary is close or a neighbour is overlooked. Atlas records no other difference between the two Combos: no areas, heights or specifications are published for either, so evidence neutrality is preserved and neither is ranked above the other. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose between the two Combos on roof form and appearance, since that is the only distinction the evidence supports — then get the overall footprint in writing.

A RECORD BLOCKED BY AN ATLAS NAMING DEFECT, NOT BY A SUPPLIER DISCLOSURE FAILURE. Gardenhouse24 publishes the Mayo Garden Black Office Box in a size ladder of XS (5 m2, 2.5 × 2.5 m), M (8.2 m2, 2.5 × 4.5 m) and L (9.5 m2, 2.8 × 4.5 m), with a Natural XL at 10.6 m2 — THERE IS NO 'S' VARIANT IN THE SUPPLIER CATALOGUE. The Atlas record therefore cannot be matched without guessing between XS and M, no figure has been attached, and nothing has been estimated. ON ANY OF THE PUBLISHED SIZES the building would sit comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: identify which size you are actually being quoted — XS, M, L or XL.

A TWO-ROOM CONTEMPORARY BOX WITH A VERIFIED 8.2 m2 INDOOR AREA AND THE HEAVIEST LOG PROFILE IN THE RANGE AT 70 mm. THE PLANNING POSITION IS COMFORTABLE: an enclosed base of 11.46 m2 including terrace sits well inside the 30 m2 combined allowance, and a flat roof at 260 cm is inside the 3 m limit. TWO ROOMS WITHIN 8.2 m2 MEANS NEITHER IS LARGE — buyers wanting a single open workspace should compare against the one-room models at similar area. DOUBLE GLAZING IN TEMPERED GLASS, PREMIUM INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL DOORS, TERRACE AND FLOOR ARE INCLUDED. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a well-specified small building whose two-room layout is the thing to think hardest about.

THE SAME BUILDING AS THE SACRAMENTO, SOLD UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME — and a homeowner should know that before choosing between them. The two are published with IDENTICAL specifications on every measured field: 28 mm walls, 292 × 292 cm envelope, 8.2 m2 floor, same ridge, wall height, overhang, roof area, roof angle and door. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE IN THE TWO TABLES IS PALLET WEIGHT. ON AREA IT IS ENTIRELY UNPROBLEMATIC: 8.53 m2 external against a 30 m2 allowance, flat roof at 210.9 cm well inside the 3 m limit. INTENDED USE IS 'STORAGE' ONLY — the manufacturer describes it as 'an ideal storage for a small and modern city garden', supplied with or without flooring. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a shed, and one you may already be looking at under another name.

THE LARGEST MODPOD — AND EXEMPT ONLY BECAUSE THE LAW CHANGED. At 26.18 m2 it sits inside the 30 m2 combined allowance with 3.82 m2 to spare, but UNDER THE PREVIOUS 25 m2 RULE THIS PRODUCT REQUIRED PLANNING PERMISSION. Anyone working from advice given before 27 July 2026 will have been told exactly that, correctly at the time. THE CERTIFIED RECORD PUTS THE CONSEQUENCE PLAINLY: newly exempt, and only just — any existing garden shed over 3.82 m2 puts you back into the permission process. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most space in the range, on the least margin, and only on a clear garden.

A LARGER EXEMPT ROOM WHERE THE MARGIN STARTS TO NARROW. 22.5 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves 7.5 m2 — and the certified record puts that precisely: enough for a SMALL existing shed but not a large one. IT WAS ALSO INSIDE THE PRE-27 JULY 2026 LIMIT of 25 m2, so the position does not depend on the change in the law. AT 22.5 m2 THE ROOM SUPPORTS TWO FUNCTIONS — workspace and gym, or studio and storage — which is the practical reason to step up from the Vaya. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a good size, and the point at which you should measure the shed before ordering.

A COMFORTABLY EXEMPT OFFICE OR GYM — 18.7 m2 WITH 11.3 m2 OF ALLOWANCE LEFT OVER. This is the ModPod model with the most planning breathing room: inside the 30 m2 combined allowance, and inside the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026 too, so nothing about its position depends on the law having changed. THE REMAINING 11.3 m2 IS ROUGHLY ONE ORDINARY SHED, which means an existing garden building is not automatically a problem. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a genuinely usable size from an Irish supplier with a published area — the most straightforward decision in this range. Sleeping accommodation would be a different consent route entirely.

THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE HERE — THE USE IS. A GUEST ROOM implies sleeping accommodation, and the Class 3 garden-structure exemption requires INCIDENTAL USE WITH NO HUMAN HABITATION: sleeping accommodation is excluded REGARDLESS OF SIZE, so obtaining the footprint would not by itself resolve this product's position. THE CLASS 3A AUXILIARY-DWELLING ROUTE may be the applicable one — 32 to 45 m2, to the rear, linked services, 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030 — but qualification is undetermined, and its 32 m2 FLOOR means a smaller unit falls between both routes with neither available. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if guests will sleep in it, this is not an exempt garden room — establish the consent route first.

A GARDEN GYM FROM A BUILDER WHO PUTS THE FOUNDATIONS INSIDE THE PRICE — which matters more for this use than any other, because FLOOR LOADING IS REAL in a room holding weights and machines, and the supplier names ground conditions as a pricing factor rather than passing the base risk to the buyer. THE ROOM IS YEAR-ROUND INSULATED to the range standard: 100 mm insulated walls, insulated roof, Kingspan floor, handed over plastered, wired and lit. THE PLANNING POSITION CANNOT BE TESTED — no area, no dimensions and no height are held, and GYM USE MAKES INTERNAL CLEAR HEIGHT DECISION-CRITICAL. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the base is handled; the height and the footprint are not published.

Best for a square garden corner where a symmetrical 497 x 497 cm building suits the plot better than a long narrow one. The 11.26 m2 enclosed room suits a single-occupant study, hobby room or seating room for seasonal use.

Best for an empty garden with no existing outbuildings, where the full 30 m2 allowance is available and a broad 592 x 502 cm envelope can be accommodated. The 14.5 m2 enclosed room suits a studio or seating room for seasonal use.

THE HIGHEST INSULATION SPECIFICATION HELD ANYWHERE IN ATLAS — 150 mm of total wall insulation: 50 mm foil-faced rigid board plus 100 mm high-density Earthwool, with a ceiling of 150 mm Earthwool plus 62 mm rigid insulated plasterboard, framed construction and solid cedar cladding. THAT EXCEEDS EVERY OTHER GARDEN ROOM SPECIFICATION CURRENTLY HELD: six times Quick-Garden's insulated Twin Skin, and above Loghouse ECO and Concept Modular. THE PLANNING POSITION CANNOT BE TESTED — no area, no dimensions and no derivable footprint are held, and nothing has been estimated, because moderngardenrooms.ie is client-rendered and returns an empty body to direct fetch. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: genuinely suitable for year-round daily office use in an Irish winter — telephone them for the footprint.

THE SECOND 'MODERN GARDEN ROOM' IN THE RANGE — AND NOTHING PUBLISHED SEPARATES IT FROM THE TRINITY. Both carry the same style designation, the same absence of a size qualifier, and the same lack of an audited area or height; EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY BETWEEN THEM IS PRESERVED DELIBERATELY. WHAT CAN BE SAID is that neither carries the elevated-risk marker applied to the four 'Large' models, so both sit in the more comfortable half of the range on the 30 m2 combined allowance. NO ROOF FORM IS RECORDED, so the applicable height limit — 3 m or 4 m — cannot be identified. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what distinguishes Clara from Trinity before anything else.

Best for a narrow garden or boundary strip only 288 cm deep, where a room approaching 10 m2 with an attached covered seating area is wanted for summer use, at the lower of the two published prices on this exact specification.

Best for a narrow garden or a boundary strip only 288 cm deep, where a small enclosed room with an attached covered seating area is wanted for summer use. The 567 cm length runs along a fence rather than across a lawn.

Best for a large garden where an 18 m2 room in a long 783 cm envelope suits a boundary run, and where the owner is prepared to clarify the planning position before ordering. At EUR 7,580 it is the lowest published price of any 18 m2 room in the catalogue.

Best for a large garden where the thickest wall specification in the supplier's range matters more than efficient use of ground, and where the owner is prepared to address planning. The 12 m2 enclosed room suits a single-purpose study or studio.

A CONTEMPORARY ROOM AT THE STANDARD SIZE BAND — the 'Modern' designation without the 'Large' marker, which is the more comfortable half of this range on the allowance. NO AUDITED AREA IS HELD AND NOTHING HAS BEEN ESTIMATED, so the 30 m2 combined test cannot be run; what can be said is that this record does not carry the elevated-risk marker applied to the large models. THE MODERN FORM RAISES THE ROOF QUESTION: a flat or mono-pitch roof is capped at 3 m rather than 4 m, and no roof form is recorded. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the footprint and the roof covering together.

THE ONE PRODUCT IN THIS RANGE BUILT ON A DIFFERENT CONSTRUCTION SYSTEM — the supplier publishes that its golf simulator rooms 'are constructed using advanced SIP panel systems that provide excellent insulation, strength, and long-term durability', rather than the 100 mm insulated timber frame used across the rest of the range. A SIP PANEL HAS NO REPEATING STUD to carry heat around the insulation, which is a meaningful internal difference. THE CONSTRAINT HERE IS HEIGHT, NOT AREA: a golf simulator needs internal clear height for a full swing, and no height is published — while the external cap is 3 m for a flat or non-tiled roof. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: internal clear height is the figure that decides this purchase, and it is not published.

THE RANGE'S STANDARD SPECIFICATION, STATED PLAINLY: 100 mm insulated walls, an insulated roof and a KINGSPAN FLOOR AS STANDARD, cedar, larch or shiplap cladding over a breather membrane, and the building HANDED OVER PLASTERED, WIRED, LIT AND READY TO FURNISH. That last point is the product — the quoted figure is a finished room, not a shell. THE PLANNING POSITION CANNOT BE TESTED: no area, no dimensions and no height are held for any product in this range, and nothing has been estimated, because the supplier's site is client-rendered and returns an empty body to direct fetch. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: winter-capable and finished as delivered — telephone for the footprint.

Best for a buyer wanting a 16 m2 room in the supplier's thickest wall specification with modest integrated storage, on a shallow 325 cm depth that suits siting along a boundary. The storage is small enough that a separate shed may still be needed for bulky items.

Best for a large garden where a 22 m2 room and substantial integrated storage are both wanted in one structure, and where the owner accepts that planning permission will be needed. The 784 x 502 cm envelope suits an open area rather than a boundary run.

Best for a large garden where covered outdoor entertaining is the main objective and a 22 m2 room supports it, and where the owner accepts that planning permission will be needed. The near-square 773 x 598 cm envelope needs an open area rather than a boundary strip.

A HOMEOWNER WHO WANTS TO CHOOSE THE SIZE RATHER THAN ACCEPT ONE — AND WHO UNDERSTANDS THAT THE CHOICE IS ALSO THE PLANNING DECISION. This record covers a stated range of 10 to 30 m2, so it can be specified small and comfortably exempt, or specified at the top and left with zero headroom against the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. That flexibility is the product's defining characteristic. WHAT IT IS NOT: a single building with a single answer. The certified AM-001 layer records that no product-level figure exists and that reading either endpoint as the area would be an inference, which has not been made. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: best for someone who will measure their existing garden structures first, subtract from 30 m2, and give the supplier the remainder as an external footprint budget — rather than choosing a size and discovering the consequence afterwards.

A HOMEOWNER WHO WANTS SIP CONSTRUCTION AND A BUILDING SIZED TO THE SITE. The certified AM-001 layer records this as a MADE-TO-ORDER product built from SIP panels, with no fixed footprint because the area is determined per commission. That combination is genuinely useful: SIPs give a continuous insulated envelope with fewer cold bridges than a stud frame, and a made-to-order footprint lets the building be specified to whatever remains of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance once existing structures are counted. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: best for someone who has measured their garden, knows their remaining allowance, and wants a warm envelope built to that number rather than a catalogue size that nearly fits. The trade is that nothing can be compared in advance — there is no published size or price to weigh against other suppliers.

A SMALL FLAT-ROOFED TIMBER BUILDING WITH A TERRACE — AND THE SUPPLIER CALLS IT A SHED. Gardenhouse24's own quality panel states its profiles 'start from 28 mm (for garden sheds)', and the page body repeatedly describes this as a garden SHED that 'can be a small home office WHEN INSULATED PROPERLY'. THE PLANNING POSITION IS EASY: a total base of 11.26 m2 including the 2.38 m2 terrace sits well inside the 30 m2 combined allowance, and a flat roof at 234.5 cm is comfortably inside the 3 m limit. THE INDOOR AREA IS 8.55 m2 — A BUYER READING THE HEADLINE '2.98 × 3.78 m' WOULD OVER-ESTIMATE THE USABLE ROOM BY ROUGHLY A THIRD. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: an 8.5 m2 room, not an 11 m2 one.

THE SMALLEST STEEL UNIT IN A RANGE WHERE EVERY MODEL CARRIES A PUBLISHED TWO-DIMENSION DESIGNATION. 9.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves roughly 20 m2 — the most generous margin of the nine Adman models — and it sat well inside the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026 as well. STEEL IS THE DIFFERENTIATOR HERE: a galvanised or coated steel building resists rot and needs no repainting, which is a real advantage in an Irish climate and a different maintenance proposition from timber. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the low-risk entry point of an Irish-made range — low maintenance, generous planning margin, and a size you can check yourself.

A STANDARD HOME OFFICE IN STEEL, WITH ROOM TO SPARE FOR A SHED. 12.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves about 17 m2 — a margin wide enough that an existing garden building is no obstacle, which is not the case further up this range. THE POSITION WAS UNCHANGED BY THE 2026 INCREASE, since 12.60 m2 sat inside the old 25 m2 limit too. FOR A BUYER WHO WANTS A DELIVERED, LOW-MAINTENANCE BUILDING rather than a design process, an Irish steel manufacturer publishing explicit dimensions is a straightforward proposition. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the size most single-occupant home offices need, with the planning question effectively settled on area.

A LONGER STEEL ROOM AT JUST OVER HALF THE ALLOWANCE. 15.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined figure leaves roughly 14 m2 — comfortable rather than tight — and the position was unchanged by the 2026 increase, since 15.60 m2 sat inside the old 25 m2 limit too. THE CERTIFIED RECORD ATTACHES A USABILITY WARNING RATHER THAN A PLANNING ONE: a 3 m depth means a long, shallow room delivers less usable working space than the same area in a squarer plan. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right choice when the garden is narrow, but do not read 15.60 m2 as equivalent to 15.60 m2 in a squarer building.

A LONG BOUNDARY-RUN BUILDING WHERE THE MARGIN STARTS TO NARROW. 18.60 m2 against the 30 m2 combined allowance leaves about 11 m2 — and the certified record puts that figure in context: 11 m2 is roughly the footprint of a single ordinary garden shed, so if the plot already holds one, the combined total needs checking rather than assuming. THE POSITION WAS UNCHANGED BY THE 2026 INCREASE, since 18.60 m2 sat inside the old 25 m2 limit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the size at which the existing contents of the garden stop being irrelevant.

A VERY LONG BOUNDARY BUILDING THAT IS EXEMPT ONLY BECAUSE THE LAW CHANGED. At 27.60 m2 it EXCEEDED the 25 m2 allowance that applied before 27 July 2026 and is inside only under the new 30 m2 limit — with under 2.40 m2 of headroom. ANYONE WHO RESEARCHED THIS PRODUCT BEFORE THAT DATE WILL HAVE BEEN TOLD, CORRECTLY AT THE TIME, THAT IT WAS NOT EXEMPT, which is worth knowing if you are relying on older advice. THE HEADROOM IS ALMOST NIL: any existing shed, garage or greenhouse takes the plot over the moment this room is added. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: viable only on a completely clear garden, and only on a verified footprint.
Homeowners who need more than one separate space in the garden — an office plus a gym or a store, for example — from a single Irish-manufactured, maintenance-free building at a mid-market price.

A PROPER MULTI-PURPOSE STEEL ROOM — 4 m OF DEPTH AND 20.80 m2 OF FLOOR. Depth is what lets a room work in two directions, and this is the size at which an office can also hold a treadmill or a workbench. AGAINST THE 30 m2 COMBINED ALLOWANCE IT LEAVES UNDER 10 m2, and the certified record marks that as the point where the margin becomes small enough to matter: a single garage or a large shed can take the plot over once this room is added. THE POSITION WAS UNCHANGED BY THE 2026 INCREASE. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the best-proportioned Adman model that still leaves any usable margin — but the garden must be measured first.

A LARGE, WELL-PROPORTIONED STEEL ROOM — AND THE MODEL THE CERTIFIED LAYERS SINGLE OUT AS THE RISKIEST IN THE RANGE. At 24.80 m2 it is inside the 30 m2 combined allowance, but only about 5.20 m2 remains for EVERY other structure in the back garden: one ordinary shed consumes most of that. IT ALSO SAT ONLY 0.20 m2 INSIDE THE PRE-27 JULY 2026 LIMIT OF 25 m2 — within the old rule by a margin narrower than any other Adman model. THE CERTIFIED RECORD DESCRIBES IT AS THE UNIT WHERE AN UNVERIFIED DESIGNATION AND A SMALL MARGIN COMBINE. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: excellent room, least tolerance for error.

A LARGE BUILDING FOR SOMEONE PREPARED TO APPLY FOR PERMISSION — THIS ONE IS NOT EXEMPT. At 36.80 m2 it exceeds the 30 m2 combined allowance by 6.80 m2 before any other structure is counted, and the 2026 increase from 25 m2 does not rescue it. THE ALTERNATIVE ROUTE IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE: 36.80 m2 does fall inside the 32–45 m2 Class 3A band, but Class 3A applies to HABITABLE accommodation linked to the principal house's services, sited to the rear, notified 14 days in advance, and expiring 31 December 2030 — a garden room is not automatically specified to meet those conditions, and no determination has been made. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: assume planning permission is required.

A SINGLE-PURPOSE WORKSPACE WHERE THE SIZE IS KNOWN BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE. NOOK publishes the area in the product name — 9.75 m2 — which is more than most of this catalogue manages, and the certified AM-006 layer places it comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with roughly 20 m2 left for anything else on the plot. It was equally inside the old 25 m2 limit, so the planning position does not depend on the 2026 change. OPEN PLAN AT THIS SIZE MEANS ONE ROOM, ONE FUNCTION: a desk and a chair, or a studio corner — not an office plus gym. THE BLOCKING QUESTION IS AVAILABILITY: NOOK is Spanish-produced and sold through an online configurator, with no published Irish installation route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: good size clarity, unresolved delivery — settle the second before you weigh the first.

A BUYER WHO NEEDS THE ROOM TO DO TWO JOBS AND WANTS THE ARITHMETIC TO BE OBVIOUS. At a published 19.5 m2 — exactly double the Base — this is a genuine dual-function space: desk plus meeting area, office plus gym, or an open studio. The certified AM-006 layer places it inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with about 10.5 m2 remaining for other structures, and it was inside the old 25 m2 limit too. THE MODULAR RELATIONSHIP IS THE USEFUL PART: because 19.5 m2 is precisely 2 x 9.75 m2, a buyer can see exactly what the step up buys, which almost no other range in this catalogue makes visible. AVAILABILITY REMAINS THE BLOCKER: Spanish production, configurator sales, no published Irish installation route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right size for two functions — if you can get it delivered and built.

THE LARGEST INTERNAL FLOOR IN THE LASITA RECORDS ATLAS HOLDS — 22.85 m2 internal on a 23.43 m2 external footprint — AND IT IS NOT A GARDEN ROOM. The manufacturer lists the intended uses for this model as 'OUTDOOR COOKING' AND 'STORAGE' ONLY; it does not list workshop or office use, which it does list for the New York. AT 28 mm THIS IS THE THINNEST WALL PROFILE IN THE LASITA CATALOGUE. ON AREA IT IS EXEMPT: inside the 30 m2 combined allowance and inside the old 25 m2 limit, though it leaves only about 6.5 m2 for every other structure. THE NEAR-FLAT ROOF at 4 degrees and a 222.3 cm ridge is comfortably inside the 3 m limit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a big, cheap, well-documented storage and outdoor-cooking building — not a workspace.

THE ONLY LASITA MAJA MODEL THE MANUFACTURER ITSELF LISTS FOR WORKSHOP AND OFFICE USE — which, of the ten products Atlas holds under Garden Rooms for this supplier, makes it the one a homeowner searching for a workspace should actually be looking at. IT IS WITHIN EXEMPTED DEVELOPMENT ON AREA: 20.40 m2 EXTERNAL footprint against a 30 m2 combined allowance, with 19.74 m2 of INTERNAL floor — both figures published and reconciling to the centimetre. THE HEIGHT DETAIL CATCHES PEOPLE OUT: the roof is pitched at 22/16 degrees but finished in SHINGLES, not tile or slate, so the applicable limit is 3 m, NOT 4 m. At a 273.6 cm ridge it clears with about 26 cm to spare. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area and on height — but by a margin, not comfortably.

THE LARGEST TIMBER LIVING MODEL — AND THE ONE WHERE THE PLANNING ARITHMETIC ACTUALLY MATTERS. All four variants sit inside the 30 m2 combined allowance: 3.50m × 2.50m (8.75 m2), 4.00m × 3.00m (12 m2), 5.00m × 3.50m (17.5 m2) and 6.00m × 4.50m (27 m2). THE LARGEST IS EXEMPT ONLY BECAUSE OF THE 27 JULY 2026 CHANGE: at 27 m2 it EXCEEDED the previous 25 m2 limit outright and now leaves just 3 m2 for every other structure. THE ROOFED FOOTPRINT IS LARGER THAN THE NOMINAL SIZE — overhangs of 1.20 m front, 0.20 m rear, 0.30 m each side. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the three smaller options are straightforward; the 6.00 × 4.50 is newly exempt and only just.

A SUMMER AND SHOULDER-SEASON ROOM AT A COMFORTABLE SIZE — 18.00 m2 nominal against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving about 12 m2 for other structures on the plot. THE 44 mm DESIGNATION IS A PLAIN LOG WALL, NOT ONE OF PINECA'S FOUR INSULATED SPECIFICATIONS, and the supplier's own guidance is unusually blunt about what that means in Ireland: 'Without proper insulation, a garden room will be cold and potentially damp for four to five months of the year – pleasant in summer but uncomfortable in autumn and winter.' HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: buy this for spring-to-autumn use with your eyes open — the supplier itself tells you what the other five months look like.

A YEAR-ROUND OFFICE AT A SIZE THAT LEAVES REAL PLANNING HEADROOM — 18.00 m2 nominal against a 30 m2 combined allowance, with about 12 m2 left for anything else on the plot. THE RECORD CARRIES PINECA'S EXPLICIT INSULATED DESIGNATION, and the supplier's own guidance for a home office used five days a week year-round is 'at minimum the 34 mm + cladding insulated specification, with SIPS or high-quality insulation for the most intensive use'. THE PLANNING TEST IS UNAFFECTED BY THE INSULATION — the regulation assesses the external footprint, which is the same 18.00 m2 across all three OAK 6 × 3 m variants. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: exempt on area with room to spare; the insulation affects what you get inside, not the planning position.

MUSICIANS AND ANYONE WHO NEEDS THE NOISE TO STAY IN THE GARDEN — BUT NOT, ON CURRENT EVIDENCE, IN IRELAND. This is a purpose-built ACOUSTICALLY ISOLATED room, constructed as a room within a room with a separate entrance lobby in the music-room configuration, and that is a genuinely different product from a garden office with thicker walls. If the requirement is drum practice, band rehearsal or recording without a neighbour dispute, nothing else in the Atlas Garden Room catalogue is built for it except Sonic Box Studios, which publishes no dimensions at all. THE BLOCKING FACT: the supplier states 'Free UK Mainland Delivery' and prices include delivery to any UK mainland address. The island of Ireland is not UK mainland, and Atlas holds no published route to purchase in either jurisdiction. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right product, wrong geography — establish whether Oeco will deliver and install in Ireland before anything else.

A TRADITIONAL SOLID-LOG CABIN FOR A GARDEN OF UNKNOWN CAPACITY — BECAUSE NOTHING ABOUT THIS PRODUCT'S SIZE IS PUBLISHED. No floor area, no dimensions, no height. THE CERTIFIED LAYERS ATTACH A WARNING SPECIFIC TO LOG CABINS: solid-log walls are thick, so if the supplier later quotes an INTERNAL floor area, the external footprint used by the planning test will be materially larger. The sister product Ontario XL sits at exactly 30 m2 on an unstated basis, and that single unanswered question is the difference between exempt and not exempt. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: whatever figure you are given, establish which side of the wall it was measured on before you do any arithmetic.

Best for a buyer who wants a separated sleeping space within a compact 24.68 m2 footprint and is prepared to resolve the planning position before ordering. The middle price point of the three Sweden fit-outs on a common shell.

A LARGE TIMBER CABIN ON A COMPLETELY CLEAR BACK GARDEN — AND ONLY THERE. At a published 30 m2 it is the largest exempt-eligible product in the catalogue, and it is inside the allowance ONLY because of the 27 July 2026 increase from 25 m2; before that date it exceeded the limit by 5 m2. IT LANDS EXACTLY ON THE LINE WITH ZERO HEADROOM. Because the 30 m2 is a COMBINED total across every structure in the back garden, ANY existing shed, garage or greenhouse takes the plot over the limit the moment this cabin is added. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the right product only if the garden is genuinely empty — and only if the supplier confirms the 30 m2 is EXTERNAL.

AN OUTDOOR-LIVING BUILDING WITH A SUBSTANTIAL COVERED AREA — AND A PLANNING POSITION THAT CANNOT BE RESOLVED FROM PUBLISHED EVIDENCE. Like the Domeo 10, the figures do not reconcile as a rectangle: 750 × 500 cm is 37.50 m2 EXTERNALLY against a 14.9 m2 enclosed floor, so a large part of the envelope is covered outdoor space that Lasita does not itemise. ON THE ENVELOPE IT EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined allowance outright. AND THE HEIGHT IS WORSE: A SUPPLIER DATA DEFECT IS RECORDED — the specification gives a WALL height of 306 cm and a RIDGE height of 244.8 cm, which is impossible. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: not exempt on area, and the height position cannot be established at all until the manufacturer resolves the contradiction.

Best for a buyer who will contact the supplier before ordering. On the published room area this is a large 24.5 m2 room in the thickest wall specification the supplier offers, with no veranda or shed taking ground; but because the published dimensions cannot contain that room, the product cannot responsibly be recommended for a specific garden until the supplier confirms its true external size.

THE SQUARE MID-SIZE OPTION — 16 m2 on the verified external footprint, WELL INSIDE the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with 14 m2 of headroom. AT THIS SIZE THE PLANNING QUESTION IS NOT A CONSTRAINT: an existing shed, a greenhouse and a future store can all coexist with it. A 4 × 4 m SQUARE IS THE MOST EFFICIENT SMALL-ROOM PLAN, with usable wall on all four sides and no wasted circulation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the safest planning position in the range at a size that still works as a full office — the remaining question is entirely about construction.

THE MOST COMFORTABLE POSITION IN THE RANGE ON THE EXEMPTION TEST — 20 m2 on the verified external footprint against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving 10 m2 of headroom. THAT IS ENOUGH FOR A SUBSTANTIAL EXISTING SHED OR A FUTURE ONE, which almost nothing above it in the range can say. A 4 × 5 m PLAN IS THE STANDARD GARDEN-ROOM PROPORTION for good reason: a desk wall, a seating end and circulation, without wasted floor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the size where the planning question stops being a constraint and the specification becomes the only thing to settle.

A SINGLE-PURPOSE ROOM ON A GARDEN THAT ALREADY HAS OTHER STRUCTURES — 15 m2 on the verified external footprint uses HALF the 30 m2 combined allowance and leaves 15 m2 for everything else. THAT IS THE MOST GENEROUS MARGIN OF ANY MID-SIZED MODEL IN THE RANGE. THE 3 m DEPTH IS THE TRADE-OFF: enough for a desk, a chair and storage along one wall, but not for a seating area opposite. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the planning question effectively disappears at this size; what remains is whether 3 m of depth suits the intended use.

THE LARGEST QUICK-GARDEN MODEL WITH A USABLE PLANNING MARGIN — 24 m2 on the verified external footprint against a 30 m2 combined allowance, leaving 6 m2. THAT IS ENOUGH FOR A MODEST EXISTING SHED and still be exempt, which the 28 m2 and 30 m2 models in the same range are not. A 6 × 4 m PLAN IS PROPERLY PROPORTIONED: 4 m of depth takes a desk wall and a seating end without becoming a corridor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on most real gardens this is the better choice than the two larger models, because the margin is what keeps the exemption intact.

THE LARGEST QUICK-GARDEN MODEL THAT STILL FITS AN ORDINARY GARDEN — BUT ONLY JUST, AND ONLY SINCE JULY 2026. 7 × 4 m is 28 m2 on the supplier's verified EXTERNAL footprint, against a 30 m2 combined allowance: 2 m2 of margin, which is smaller than almost any garden shed. UNDER THE PRE-27-JULY-2026 25 m2 RULE THIS PRODUCT REQUIRED PLANNING PERMISSION; it is exempt only because of the increase. THE 4 m DEPTH IS GENEROUS — enough for a desk wall and a seating area rather than a corridor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a genuinely large room, exempt on a clear plot and not on a built-on one; audit the whole garden before ordering.

THE SMALLEST PRODUCT IN THE ATLAS QUICK-GARDEN SET AND THE ONE WHERE AREA IS SIMPLY NOT AN ISSUE — 2 × 2 m is 4 m2 on the supplier's verified external footprint, roughly an eighth of the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance. IT FITS ALONGSIDE ALMOST ANYTHING ALREADY IN A GARDEN. FOUR SQUARE METRES IS A DESK, A CHAIR AND A DOOR: a single-occupant focus pod rather than a room. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the planning question is answered before it is asked; the live questions are what it is made of and whether four square metres is enough.

THE MOST COMFORTABLY EXEMPT MODEL IN THE TIMBER LIVING RANGE — all four variants sit well inside the 30 m2 combined allowance: 3.0m × 2.0m (6 m2), 3.5m × 3.0m (10.5 m2), 4.0m × 3.5m (14 m2) and 4.5m × 4.0m (18 m2), leaving AT LEAST 12 m2 OF HEADROOM even on the largest. IT IS ALSO THE MODEL WHOSE LABELS CAN BE TRUSTED: the supplier's technical sketch for the smallest option is captioned 300 × 200, exactly matching the label — the opposite of the Havana. A LOW-PITCH MODERN ROOF AND FULL FRONT GLAZING give it a contemporary line. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the easiest planning position in the range; the wall specification is the open question.

THE ENTRY MODEL OF BERTILO'S SECOND PENT-ROOF LINE — AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD SETS OUT THE POSITION PLAINLY. A pent, or mono-pitch, roof is NOT a tiled or slated pitched roof, so the 3 m height limit applies rather than 4 m. Bertilo model numerals are nominal names, NOT m2. No audited area is held, and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor. THE CERTIFIED LAYER DESCRIBES THE AREA QUESTION AS 'CURRENTLY MOOT' for exactly that reason: with no purchasing route, the test cannot arise. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a clean contemporary form, and no way for an Irish buyer to obtain it.

THE SECOND STEP IN A SEVEN-RECORD PENT-ROOF LINE — AND THE STEP ITSELF IS UNQUANTIFIED. The certified layers record Bertilo numerals as nominal names rather than square metres, so nothing separates this from the Pent Modern 1 on evidence, and evidence neutrality between them is preserved deliberately. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED APPLIES TO THE WHOLE LINE: a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so the 3 m height limit applies; no audited area is held; and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the roof form is the only thing the name reliably tells you.

THE 'PLUS' VERSION OF THE SECOND PENT MODERN — AND THE SUFFIX HAS NO RECORDED MEANING. Nothing in the certified layers says whether Plus denotes extra size, extra specification or extra equipment, and none of those has been inferred. THE ROOF FORM IS THE ONE THING SETTLED: a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so the 3 m limit applies rather than 4 m. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor — which the certified record describes as making the area question currently moot. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: 'Plus' is the word to have itemised in writing.

THE THIRD NUMERAL IN THE PENT MODERN LINE — AND, AS THROUGHOUT BERTILO, THE NUMERAL IS A NAME RATHER THAN A SIZE. Nothing published establishes that this model is larger than the Pent Modern 2, and no such reading has been made. THE LINE'S CONSTANTS APPLY: a pent roof caps the height at 3 m rather than 4 m; no audited area is held; Estonia-only shipping with no Irish distributor, which the certified record notes makes the area test moot in practice. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: within this line, the only reliable differentiator is the roof form — which is identical across all seven records.

THE UPGRADED VERSION OF THE THIRD PENT MODERN — TWO UNDEFINED MODIFIERS ON ONE PRODUCT. The numeral is a nominal name rather than a size, and the Plus suffix has no recorded content, so a buyer choosing this over the plain Pent Modern 3 is paying for a distinction the catalogue cannot describe. THE ROOF FORM IS THE ONE FIXED POINT: a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched, so 3 m applies rather than 4 m. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD; Estonia-only shipping, no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two questions for the supplier — what size, and what does Plus add.

THE TOP NUMERAL OF THE PENT MODERN LINE — AND THE CERTIFIED RECORD CALLS THE AREA QUESTION 'CURRENTLY MOOT'. That is not a dismissal: with Estonia-only shipping and no Irish distributor, there is no route by which an Irish homeowner could buy this, so the 30 m2 test never arises in practice. IF IT DID, IT COULD NOT BE RUN: no audited area is held and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size. THE ROOF FORM IS SETTLED — a pent roof caps the height at 3 m rather than 4 m. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the largest model in the line, and the one furthest from being purchasable here.

THE TOP OF THE LINE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — highest numeral, Plus tier — AND NEITHER DESIGNATION IS DEFINED ANYWHERE. The certified layers record numerals as nominal names rather than square metres, and nothing describes what Plus adds; both readings have been refused rather than inferred. THE ROOF FORM REMAINS THE ONE SETTLED CONDITION: pent, therefore capped at 3 m rather than 4 m. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, and Estonia-only shipping means the area test is moot for an Irish buyer. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the range's flagship, and the record with the least published behind it.

A PENT-ROOFED HOME OFFICE — THE CONFIGURATION WITH THE CLEANEST PLANNING POSITION IN THE RANGE. Office use is incidental to the enjoyment of the house, so the use condition is satisfied outright; and the pent roof settles the height test at 3 m rather than 4 m. THAT IS TWO OF THE FOUR CONDITIONS ANSWERED FROM THE PRODUCT NAME ALONE, which no other Bertilo record manages. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: no audited area and no published height, so neither figure can be checked, and the numeral is a nominal name. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the clearest Bertilo record on use, still silent on measurement.

A PENT-ROOFED POOLHOUSE — CHANGING AND STORAGE BESIDE A POOL, IN THE RANGE'S CONTEMPORARY FORM. The certified record carries the poolhouse caution: a building serving a swimming pool may raise separate considerations beyond the garden-structure tests. THE ROOF FORM SETTLES THE HEIGHT LIMIT at 3 m rather than 4 m, since a pent roof is not tiled or slated pitched — useful, because a poolhouse is a low building where that cap is unlikely to bind. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, and shipping is Estonia-only. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the form suits the use; the figures still have to be obtained.

THE LARGEST PENT-ROOFED OFFICE IN THE RANGE — for two people working, or one with equipment. AS WITH ITS SMALLER SIBLING, two conditions are settled by the name: office use is incidental and therefore permitted, and the pent roof caps the height at 3 m rather than 4 m. THE TWO MEASURABLE TESTS REMAIN OPEN: no audited area and no published height, and the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size, so it is not confirmed that this office is larger than the Pentus 2 Office. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the biggest office in a line with no published sizes — the footprint is the whole question.

THE LARGEST POOLHOUSE BERTILO OFFERS — pent-roofed, top numeral, for a pool used by a family rather than a couple. The certified record repeats the poolhouse caution and adds the range's standing one: Bertilo model numerals are NOMINAL NAMES, NOT m2, so it is not established that this is larger than the Pentus 2 Poolhouse at all. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so the 30 m2 combined test and the 3 m pent-roof cap cannot be checked. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on a developed pool site, the footprint is the figure that decides everything.

CANNOT BE MATCHED TO A REQUIREMENT — THE ONE NUMBER IN THE NAME IS NOT A SIZE. The certified AM-001 layer records that the numeral 17 may denote 17 m2 or may be a model number, that Atlas holds no evidence establishing which, and that reading it as an area would be an inference which has NOT been made. A prior session found numeric model suffixes across this catalogue to be nominal names rather than areas, so the caution is well founded rather than pedantic. WITH NO CONFIRMED AREA AND NO PUBLISHED HEIGHT, nothing can be said about who the Studio suits: not its usable space, not its planning position, not its value. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the single most useful question you can ask The Pod Factory is whether 17 is square metres or a model number — that one answer would make this record comparable.

A HOUSEHOLD THAT NEEDS SLEEPING ACCOMMODATION IN THE GARDEN — AND THAT CHANGES THE WHOLE PROJECT. The supplier's own designation is ONE-BED, and the certified AM-006 layer records that a one-bed garden pod is sleeping accommodation, which falls outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption on use ALONE, at any floor area. So the useful framing is not 'which pod is bigger' but 'which consent route applies'. THE ROUTE THAT MIGHT APPLY, the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling exemption, runs from 32 m2 to 45 m2 — and it cannot be tested here because no area is published; the numeral 22 has not been read as 22 m2. If it were 22 m2, the pod would fall BELOW the Class 3A minimum and qualify under neither route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right product only for someone prepared to treat this as a dwelling proposal and talk to their planning office first.

BEST FOR AN ENGLISH BUYER WHO FIRST ESTABLISHES WHICH MODEL THEY ARE ACTUALLY BUYING — the certified thermal layer records an unresolved identity question on this record and it comes before everything else. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the Booths studio specification, published Tier A — 90 mm ECOTHERM floor insulation, 90 mm ACTIS in walls and ceiling, A-rated double glazing described as thermally equivalent to triple glazing, 75 mm galvanised steel-clad panels, corrugated bitumen roof, 25-YEAR STRUCTURAL GUARANTEE, and NO CONCRETE BASE REQUIRED — the building sits on an adjustable chassis on composite feet. For gym use the range publishes two directly relevant options: a DECOUPLED FLOOR to accommodate movement, which the supplier states helps with treadmills and cross-trainers, and an EXTENDED INTERNAL HEIGHT of 7 ft 10 in, described as popular with home gyms running tall machines. THE IDENTITY PROBLEM: no QC8 appears in the supplier's current published range — its FAQ names the QCB5, the QC9 and the Annexe only — so this may be a SUPERSEDED specification. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE: England-only delivery. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: confirm the model, then the height.

THE FIRST BOOTHS MODEL THAT IS A ROOM RATHER THAN A BOOTH. At approximately 7.43 m2 on the supplier's 8 × 10 ft designation it holds a desk, a chair for someone else and some storage — the point at which a garden office becomes a workplace rather than a refuge. IT LEAVES ROUGHLY 22 m2 OF THE COMBINED ALLOWANCE for existing structures, so the planning arithmetic remains untroubled. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: for the modest step up from the 6 × 8 ft models, this is the size most people who work from home will actually be satisfied with.

THE SMALLEST GARDEN OFFICE IN THE CATALOGUE — A SINGLE DESK AND NOTHING ELSE. At approximately 4.46 m2 on the supplier's 6 × 8 ft designation it uses under a sixth of the 30 m2 combined allowance, and the certified record is unusually direct about what follows: AREA IS NOWHERE NEAR THE BINDING CONSTRAINT HERE. What matters instead is height, siting behind the front wall of the house, and keeping the use incidental. FOR A BUYER WHO NEEDS SOMEWHERE TO SHUT THE DOOR ON WORK and has a small garden, that is a genuinely simple proposition. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: no planning arithmetic required — check the siting and the roof height instead.

A HOME GYM — AND THE ONE MODEL IN THE RANGE WHERE ATLAS CAN SAY NOTHING ABOUT SIZE. The certified AM-001 layer records NO AREA PUBLISHED: no floor area, no dimensions, no derivable footprint. ITS SIBLING QCB5 RECORDS CARRY A 6 × 8 ft NOMINAL, BUT CARRYING THAT FIGURE ACROSS WOULD BE AN INFERENCE AND IT HAS NOT BEEN MADE. HEIGHT IS EQUALLY LIVE: gym use makes internal clear height decision-critical, and the 3 m external limit for a flat or non-tiled roof constrains it directly. No height is held either. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get both the footprint and the internal clear height in writing before ordering.

THE SAME SMALL SHELL AS THE QCB5 OFFICE, SOLD FOR A DIFFERENT PURPOSE — AND THE PURPOSE IS THE RISK. At approximately 4.46 m2 the area test is not close to binding, but the certified record attaches a specific caution: the model is named a RETREAT, and the exemption holds only while use stays incidental to the house AND NO ONE SLEEPS IN IT. A retreat used as a garden reading room is exempt; the same building used as occasional guest accommodation is not, at any size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on this product the area is irrelevant and the use is everything — be clear about it before ordering.

UK homeowners who want the garden itself to be part of the room. The QuadPod is designed around a large fixed viewing window specifically to maximise light and outlook, which makes it the Sanctum range to choose when the view matters as much as the floor space.

UK homeowners with very little garden who still want a fully insulated, fully installed, properly wired room rather than a shed with a heater. At 1.8m x 1.8m nominal this is the smallest Sanctum product in Atlas and is squarely a single-desk office.

CANNOT BE MATCHED TO A HOMEOWNER, AND THERE IS A SECOND UNRESOLVED QUESTION BEHIND THE FIRST. Like the rest of this supplier's records it is a COLLECTION rather than a building, with no area, dimensions, height or price, so nothing can be tested. THE NAME ALSO RAISES A USE QUESTION: 'Abode' suggests dwelling accommodation, and habitable use is excluded from the Class 3 garden-structure exemption at any size — but nothing in the supplier material Atlas holds establishes whether any model in this collection is intended for habitation, and no reading has been assumed. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: two questions come before any other — which models make up the collection, and are any of them intended to be lived in.

CANNOT BE MATCHED TO A HOMEOWNER — A THIRD COLLECTION WITH THE SAME EVIDENCE POSITION AS THE OTHER TWO. No area, dimensions, height, specification, warranty or price is held, and the record points at the same category page as the Studio and Abode collections. NOTHING DISTINGUISHES THE THREE IN ATLAS, so evidence neutrality is preserved and no ranking has been created between them; in particular, 'Luxuriance' has not been read as denoting a premium tier. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the choice between Quinn Offsite's three collections cannot be made from published information at all — ask the supplier what separates them, in writing.

CANNOT BE MATCHED TO A HOMEOWNER — THE RECORD IS A COLLECTION, NOT A BUILDING. The certified AM-001 layer states that no single footprint exists to record even in principle, and that the URL held is a category page covering a family of models. A collection name cannot be tested against a requirement: it says nothing about size, height, specification or price. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if Quinn Offsite appeals, the first request is the model list — names, external footprints and heights — after which each model can be compared properly against the documented products in this catalogue. Until then this entry is a starting point for an enquiry rather than a candidate.

THE CLEANEST MEASUREMENT DISCLOSURE FOUND ANYWHERE IN THE GARDEN ROOM CATALOGUE. Gardenhouse24 publishes the external base, the internal room dimensions AND the indoor area, and all three reconcile exactly: 400 × 600 cm less 70 mm of log on each of four sides gives 386 × 586 cm, which is 22.62 m2 precisely as stated. THERE IS NO AMBIGUITY LEFT TO RESOLVE. ON PLANNING: an enclosed base of 24.00 m2 sits inside the 30 m2 combined allowance — and inside the old 25 m2 limit too — leaving about 6 m2 for anything else. THE FLAT ROOF AT 256.5 cm clears the 3 m limit with roughly 43 cm of margin. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: everything the exemption test needs is published and checks out.

CANNOT BE DETERMINED — THE RECORD NAMES AN ENTRY RANGE, NOT A BUILDING. No floor area, dimensions, specification, warranty or price is held for this record, and the certified AM-001 and AM-006 layers both record that nothing has been estimated. An 'entry range' label tells a buyer only that the supplier has cheaper and dearer options, which is true of almost every company in this catalogue and is not a basis for a recommendation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this record cannot be shortlisted or compared as it stands. If Rayco appeals, ask for the specific model names, their external dimensions and what the entry price includes — and note the attribution caution below before relying on anything you are sent.
A single-room garden office or studio at 16.9m² — enough for a desk plus seating rather than a desk alone — for a homeowner arranging their own base, electrics and assembly.

Homeowners who want serious insulation performance at the lowest entry price in this review, and who have their own builder or electrician lined up. This is a SIPS kit, not a finished room — the price reflects that honestly.

A one-person garden office for a homeowner who already has a builder and electrician arranged. At 12.1m² it is the second-smallest SIPS-House model, and it buys a genuinely high-performance envelope at a price normally associated with basic timber sheds.

The value pick of the SIPS-House range. At 20.8m² from EUR 9,990 it delivers roughly EUR 480 per m² — the lowest cost per square metre of any SIPS-House model — in Nordic Thermowood cladding. Best for a homeowner who wants real space and a strong envelope and will arrange their own base and electrics.

A two-bedroom garden dwelling at 48.4m² — the largest SIPS-House model in Atlas. Best for a homeowner creating genuine independent accommodation who is running it as a full construction project with planning and services.

A one-bedroom garden annexe at 41.2m² — this is accommodation, not a garden office. Best for a homeowner housing a family member or creating a rental unit who will run the planning application and services connection themselves.
A large single-space garden room at 24.8m² — big enough for a combined office and gym, or a studio with a seating area — for a homeowner managing their own base, electrics and assembly.
