A LONG, NARROW BUILDING FOR A GARDEN WITH NOTHING ELSE IN IT — AND THAT SECOND CONDITION IS ABSOLUTE. At 3 × 10 m the external footprint is 30 m2, sitting EXACTLY ON the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with ZERO HEADROOM. Any existing shed, store or garage takes the combined total over and planning permission is required. IT IS ALSO EXEMPT ONLY BECAUSE OF THE 27 JULY 2026 INCREASE from 25 m2; before that date it was over the limit outright. THE 3 m DEPTH IS THE REAL DESIGN POINT: a 10 m run along a boundary intrudes far less into a garden than a square building of the same area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: viable only on a clear plot, and the height and roof covering must be confirmed as well.

THE BEST-EVIDENCED BUILDING IN THE QUICK-GARDEN RANGE. 18 m2 on the verified external footprint leaves 12 m2 of the 30 m2 combined allowance, and Atlas holds BOTH internal and external dimensions for it — internal 571 × 271 cm against external 300 × 600 cm, which is what confirmed the supplier's headline areas are external. IT ALSO HOLDS A PRODUCT-SPECIFICALLY VERIFIED INSULATED BUILD-UP: wall 44 mm + 25 mm insulation + 44 mm, roof and floor 20 mm tongue-and-groove + 25 mm insulation, in slow-grown spruce. THE MINIMUM BASE IS PUBLISHED at 284 × 584 cm. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: more of this building is documented than of anything else in the range.

A SMALL, MODERN, FLAT-ROOFED TIMBER STORE — and the manufacturer is explicit that storage is what it is for. Lasita lists 'STORAGE' as the ONLY intended use, describes it as 'an ideal storage in a modern garden', sizes the door for lawnmowers and wheelbarrows, and offers it WITH OR WITHOUT FLOORING. At 28 mm walls, no glazing beyond narrow lights and no floor as standard, THIS IS A SHED. ON AREA IT IS COMPLETELY UNPROBLEMATIC: 8.53 m2 external against a 30 m2 combined allowance, with 8.2 m2 internal, and a flat roof at 210.9 cm far inside the 3 m limit. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: an excellent small store; it should not be compared against year-round workspaces.

A HOUSEHOLD THAT WANTS A GENUINELY LARGE MULTI-USE ROOM AND IS PREPARED TO APPLY FOR PERMISSION. At 5.2 m × 6 m the certified layers record 31.20 m2 nominal — the largest Shanette product in Atlas and big enough for gym equipment AND a table, which is precisely what 'Gym & Games Room' promises. THE TRADE IS EXPLICIT AND UNAVOIDABLE: 31.20 m2 EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance by 1.20 m2 on its own, before any existing shed or garage is counted, so the certified AM-006 layer classifies it as over the exemption limit. This is not a marginal technicality that a tidy garden can fix. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right product for the space you want, wrong product if you want to avoid a planning application — and the sister Home Gym at 24.80 m2 is the exempt alternative from the same range.

A HOME GYM THAT IS ACTUALLY BIG ENOUGH TO TRAIN IN, AND STILL EXEMPT ON AREA. At a supplier designation of 6.2 m × 4 m the certified layers record 24.80 m2 nominal — room for a rack, a bench and floor space, which the 9 to 12 m2 pods elsewhere in this catalogue cannot offer. The certified AM-006 layer places it inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance, and it was inside the old 25 m2 limit too, by 0.20 m2. A HOME GYM IS ALSO CLEANLY INCIDENTAL USE, so unlike the habitable products in this Atlas there is no use exclusion to work around. THE CATCH IS THE HEADROOM: 24.80 m2 leaves only about 5.20 m2 of the combined allowance for every other structure in the garden. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right size for serious training on a clear plot — measure any existing shed before ordering.

A TRADITIONALLY STYLED GARDEN ROOM DESIGNED AND BUILT IN IRELAND — AND, LIKE ITS CONTEMPORARY COUNTERPART, A RANGE RATHER THAN A PRODUCT. The certified layers record that no single footprint exists to test even in principle: the area question belongs to whichever model is built. FOR A HOMEOWNER IN AN OLDER OR MORE TRADITIONAL SETTING, a classic pitched form has a practical planning advantage the certified layers make explicit — a TILED OR SLATED PITCHED ROOF carries a 4 m height limit rather than the 3 m that applies to flat and non-tiled roofs. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the traditional roof is not only an aesthetic choice; it may be the one that keeps a taller building inside the exemption.

A DESIGN-LED GARDEN ROOM FROM AN ESTABLISHED IRISH SUPPLIER — BUT THIS RECORD IS A RANGE, NOT A PRODUCT. The certified layers record that as a catalogue issue: no single footprint exists to test even in principle, because the area test applies to whichever specific model is built. THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS — a planning statement about 'the Contemporary Range' cannot be relied upon for any individual build. WHAT THE RANGE OFFERS is a contemporary aesthetic with Irish design, survey and installation, which for most homeowners is worth more than a published specification from a supplier who cannot visit the site. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose the model first; every planning figure follows from that.

A DEDICATED HOME CINEMA IN THE GARDEN, FROM AN ESTABLISHED IRISH SUPPLIER — AND ON THIS PRODUCT THE USE IS NOT THE PROBLEM. A home cinema used by the household is INCIDENTAL USE, so it sits squarely inside what the Class 3 exemption permits, which is more than can be said for several habitable-looking products in this catalogue. THE LIVE RISKS ARE AREA AND HEIGHT, and Shomera publishes neither: no floor area, no dimensions, no overall height. SHOMERA'S IRISH BASE IS THE REAL ADVANTAGE HERE — the questions can be put to a local supplier who builds under Irish rules. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right use, the right jurisdiction, and two figures you must ask for.

A GOLF SIMULATOR BAY — THE CLEAREST CASE IN THIS CATALOGUE OF A BUILDING WHOSE PLANNING RISK IS HEIGHT, NOT AREA. The certified record states it directly: simulator use imposes a minimum ceiling height and swing clearance, so the 3 m Class 3 limit for a flat or non-tiled roof is LIKELY TO BE THE BINDING CONSTRAINT rather than the 30 m2 allowance. A bay needs height for a full swing plus screen and projector, and once the floor build-up and roof structure are added the overall height can pass 3 m on a footprint comfortably inside the allowance. NEITHER FIGURE IS PUBLISHED. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: lead with the height question on this product — the area may never be what stops you.

A HOME SPIN OR CYCLE ROOM — AND A PRODUCT WHERE HEIGHT IS AS DECISIVE AS AREA. The certified record is explicit: spin and cycle studio use imposes CEILING-HEIGHT AND VENTILATION requirements, so internal clear height drives the overall build height, and a building designed around standing cycling clearance plus a ventilation void can approach the 3 m flat-roof limit quickly. A HOME GYM OR SPIN ROOM IS INCIDENTAL USE, so the use condition is satisfied — the risk is purely dimensional, and neither the height nor the footprint is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a product to specify from the roofline down, not from the floor plan out.

A SELF-ASSEMBLY GARDEN ROOM AT THE SMALL END — THE ONE RECORD IN THIS RANGE THAT NAMES ITS INSTALLATION MODEL. 'DIY' tells a buyer that the building arrives as a kit to be put up rather than installed, which changes the cost, the timeline and where responsibility sits if something is wrong — and no other Hansa24 record states this either way. ON PLANNING, the position is the range's: no audited area is held and nothing estimated, though a small model is the least likely to threaten the 30 m2 combined allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a kit is cheaper and slower; budget for a weekend and a second pair of hands.

Best for a small garden or a site where the statutory allowance is already partly used, and where a plain 9 m2 room is wanted with no covered outdoor space. Almost all the ground given up becomes usable room.

Best for a very small garden, a courtyard, or a site where the statutory allowance is nearly used up, and where a single desk and chair is all that is needed. At 4.7 to 5 m2 this is a one-person booth rather than a room, and the buyer must be willing to establish the wall specification themselves.

Best for a single-occupant home office on a medium garden, where the smallest member of the Hansa Lounge family suits the plot and the owner will establish what the published envelope contains before ordering. The near-square 447 x 397 cm plan suits a corner.

THE SMALL END OF A RANGE WHOSE RISK IS CONCENTRATED AT THE LARGE END. Where Hansa24's 'Large' models carry an elevated-risk marker against the 30 m2 allowance, a model explicitly designated SMALL sits at the opposite end of that scale — and although no audited area is held and nothing has been estimated, a small building is the least likely in any range to threaten the combined limit. THE LETTER 'B' IS REUSED ACROSS DIFFERENT HANSA24 PRODUCTS, so the SKU must govern any quotation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the lowest-risk shape of purchase in this range, with the footprint still worth confirming.

Best for a buyer wanting the cheapest way into a small enclosed garden room, on a site where the statutory allowance is already partly used. Suited to summer storage, a hobby space or occasional seating rather than year-round work.

Best for an open garden position where a near-square structure suits the plot, and where covered outdoor seating with a small enclosed room attached is the objective. The 58 mm wall is thicker than most small models in the range.

Best for a household whose objective is a large covered outdoor sitting area with a small lockable store attached, rather than a garden room in the usual sense. The 6.5 m2 enclosed space suits garden furniture, tools or a bar rather than a desk.

A FIRST STEP INTO ACOUSTIC ISOLATION — THE ENTRY TIER OF A PURPOSE-BUILT STUDIO RANGE. Sonic Box builds room-within-a-room studios, which is a genuinely different product from a garden office with thicker walls: the isolated inner shell is what stops structure-borne sound reaching a neighbour. 'Entry' denotes the acoustic specification level, not a size, and the certified AM-001 layer records that explicitly. AVAILABILITY IS THE BLOCKER: sonicboxstudios.co.uk is a UK domain, Sussex-based, with no evidence of an Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right category for a noise problem, unresolved geography for an Irish buyer.

THE SECOND ACOUSTIC TIER, AND ATLAS CANNOT SAY WHAT THAT BUYS. 'Standard' denotes a specification level rather than a size, and no isolation rating, dimension, height or price is published for any tier — so the step up from Entry cannot be quantified from evidence, and no ranking between the four models has been created beyond the order the supplier itself states. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY IS PRESERVED DELIBERATELY. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the same room-within-a-room construction, and the same absence of an Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask Sonic Box what each tier delivers in decibels — that is the only figure that distinguishes them.

THE THIRD ACOUSTIC TIER — AND THE CERTIFIED LAYER WARNS AGAINST THE OBVIOUS ASSUMPTION. AM-001 records that 'Enhanced' denotes an acoustic specification level, NOT a size, and has not been treated as one. A higher tier may mean thicker isolation rather than a bigger building, or both; nothing published distinguishes them on floor area. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not read Entry, Standard, Enhanced and Pro as a size ladder. If you need a larger room as well as better isolation, that has to be established separately — and no dimensions are published for any tier.

THE TOP ACOUSTIC TIER — FOR A SEMI-PROFESSIONAL REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A DOMESTIC ONE. The certified AM-001 layer records that 'Pro' is an acoustic specification tier, not a size, and has not been read as one. For someone recording commercially at home, teaching several pupils a day, or rehearsing a full band, the highest isolation level in a purpose-built range is the correct starting point. THE SAME TWO GAPS APPLY AS ACROSS THE RANGE: no dimensions, no height and no Irish purchasing route. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right tier for a demanding user, but the specification still has to be obtained in correspondence.

Best for a large garden where a near-square 639 x 616 cm structure can sit in the open, combining a 25.3 m2 room with a substantial covered veranda, and where the owner is prepared to go through planning and to ask what the price premium over comparable models represents.

THE SMALLEST UNIT IN THE RANGE AND THE ONE LEAST LIKELY TO TROUBLE THE ALLOWANCE — a 2 m designation against a 30 m2 combined back-garden limit. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE, because Sprout Pod publishes ONE DIMENSION ONLY across its entire range, so the area test cannot be run on held data and nothing has been estimated. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS EVERYTHING ELSE: an Irish manufacturer in Dundalk, free delivery and free installation across the Republic and Northern Ireland, turnkey finish with sockets, lights, HEATING and flooring included, no crane and NO CONCRETE FOUNDATION required. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a desk-and-chair office, delivered wired and heated, with no groundworks and no realistic planning exposure.

A SMALL CONTEMPORARY POD IN COMPOSITE CLADDING RATHER THAN TIMBER — the material choice is the real difference here, and it is a maintenance decision as much as an aesthetic one. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: Sprout Pod publishes a single dimension only across all 25 products, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested and nothing has been estimated. AT 3 m THIS IS AT THE SMALL END, where area is unlikely to be the binding constraint. A SLIDING DOOR ALSO NEEDS NO SWING SPACE, which matters on a small pod against a boundary. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for both dimensions, but the practical questions here are finish and door type.

A SMALL POD WITH A SHELTERED OUTDOOR EDGE — the extended canopy is the distinguishing feature, and it is also the one that complicates the planning question. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: the range is published with a single dimension only, and nothing has been estimated. ADDITIONAL AMBIGUITY IS RECORDED HERE SPECIFICALLY: the canopy is NOT STATED to fall inside the quoted 3 m, and A ROOFED CANOPY MAY ITSELF COUNT toward the 30 m2 combined allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask whether the canopy is inside or outside the quoted 3 m, because the answer changes what is counted — that is a different question from the one the other pods raise.

THE PLAINEST OF THE THREE 3 m PODS — timber cladding, a sliding door and a window, with no canopy and no integral store to complicate the area question. THAT SIMPLICITY IS THE USEFUL THING: everything roofed is the pod itself. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE, since Sprout Pod publishes a single dimension across all 25 products, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested and nothing has been estimated — but at 3 m the area is unlikely to be the binding constraint. A SEPARATE WINDOW ALONGSIDE THE DOOR gives cross-light in a small room. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: request both dimensions, then add any existing shed — the arithmetic here is as simple as it gets in this range.

A 4 m POD THAT OPENS ALONG MOST OF ITS FRONT — bifold doors fold back rather than swing, so the room can be opened up without giving away floor to a door arc. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: Sprout Pod publishes one dimension only across all 25 products, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested and nothing has been estimated. AT 4 m THE AREA IS UNLIKELY TO BE THE BINDING CONSTRAINT on a clear plot, though that cannot be confirmed without the width. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THE PACKAGE: Irish manufacture, free nationwide delivery and installation, turnkey finish with heating included. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: request both dimensions before assuming exemption, and add anything already in the garden.

THE MIDDLE OF THE RANGE AND THE MOST ORDINARY REQUIREMENT IT SERVES — a 4 m pod in Siberian larch with French doors, no store and no canopy, so everything roofed is the room itself. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: the range is published with one dimension only, nothing has been estimated, and the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested on held data. AT 4 m THE AREA IS UNLIKELY TO BIND unless the garden already carries structures, but that cannot be confirmed without the width. FRENCH DOORS OPEN THE ROOM TO THE GARDEN in a way sliding doors do not. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: request both dimensions, then add anything already standing.

A HOUSEHOLD THAT NEEDS A WORKSPACE AND STORAGE AND DOES NOT WANT TWO BUILDINGS — the integral store is the point of this configuration, and combining them is usually the better use of a garden. BUT THE STORE IS NOT FREE SPACE ON THE PLANNING TEST: storage built into the unit COUNTS TOWARD THE SAME 30 m2 COMBINED ALLOWANCE, exactly as a separate shed would. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE, since the range is published with one dimension only and nothing has been estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the TOTAL external footprint including the store, not the room dimension alone — that is the figure the exemption is tested against.

A 5 m ROOM IN COMPOSITE RATHER THAN NATURAL TIMBER, WITH FRENCH DOORS — the composite finish is the distinguishing feature and it is a maintenance choice as much as an appearance one. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: one dimension is published for every product in the range, and at 5 m the certified layer records that the second dimension decides the exemption. Nothing has been estimated. THE CONFIGURATION IS OTHERWISE PLAIN — no store, no canopy — so everything roofed is the room. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the width in writing settles the planning; the finish settles the next twenty years.

A COMPOSITE-CLAD 5 m ROOM WITH SLIDING DOORS — the low-maintenance finish combined with the opening that takes no swing space, which suits a building set close to a boundary or a path. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: the range publishes one dimension only, and at 5 m the certified layer records that the second dimension decides the exemption; nothing has been estimated. NO STORE AND NO CANOPY, so everything roofed is the room itself. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: on published evidence this differs from the composite teak French-door version only in the opening — choose on how the doors will be used, and get the width in writing.

THE MOST ENCLOSED CONFIGURATION AT 5 m — a letterbox window rather than a glazed front, which changes what the room is for. LIGHT WITHOUT EXPOSURE IS A REAL BRIEF: a studio, a music room, a workshop or an office where a screen must be readable and passers-by should not see in. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE, and at 5 m the unpublished width decides the exemption — nothing has been estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the 5 m pod to choose when privacy or wall space matters more than a view; the width still has to be obtained in writing.

A 5 m ROOM THAT OPENS ALONG ITS FRONT — the widest opening the range offers, at the size where it has most effect. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: Sprout Pod publishes a single dimension across all 25 products, and at 5 m the certified layer records that the second dimension DECIDES THE ANSWER, since a 5 m × 6 m unit would exceed the 30 m2 combined allowance outright. Nothing has been estimated. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THAT THIS IS A ROOM YOU LIVE IN RATHER THAN WORK IN ONLY, delivered finished with heating, sockets, lights and flooring, by an Irish manufacturer with free nationwide installation. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a summer-facing room — get the width in writing before ordering.

A FULL-SIZED GARDEN ROOM IN THE RANGE'S MOST COMMON CLADDING, WITH THE RANGE'S MOST COMMON DOOR. At a 5 m length the second dimension decides the exemption and no width is published, so the 30 m2 combined allowance cannot be tested and nothing has been estimated. THE CONFIGURATION IS OTHERWISE THE SIMPLEST IN THE BAND — no store, no canopy, so everything roofed is the room. FRENCH DOORS OPEN THE ROOM TO A LAWN rather than to a path. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: at 5 m the width is the whole planning question; get it in writing before ordering.

THE POINT WHERE THE MISSING WIDTH STARTS TO MATTER. At a 5 m length the second dimension decides the exemption outright — 5 m × 6 m WOULD EXCEED THE 30 m2 ALLOWANCE, and nothing published gives the width. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE and nothing has been estimated. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THAT THIS IS A FULL ROOM RATHER THAN A POD, in the range's most common cladding, with sliding doors that take no swing space — useful when a 5 m building is set close to a boundary. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the width in writing before ordering; at this size band it is no longer a formality.

THE SAME 5 m BIFOLD CONFIGURATION AS THE SIBERIAN LARCH VERSION, IN TEAK CLADDING — and on published evidence the cladding is the only difference between them. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: the range carries a single dimension only, and at 5 m the certified layer records that the second dimension decides the exemption. Nothing has been estimated. TEAK IS A WARMER, DARKER FINISH than larch and weathers differently, which is an aesthetic decision the catalogue supports and does not quantify. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: choose between larch and teak on looks; the planning question is identical and still open.

A 5 m TEAK ROOM WITH CONCEALED STORAGE AND FRENCH DOORS ONTO THE GARDEN — the same combination as its sliding-door sibling, differing only in the opening. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE: one dimension is published, nothing has been estimated, and THE HIDDEN STORE COUNTS TOWARD THE SAME 30 m2 COMBINED ALLOWANCE as the room. At 5 m the second dimension is already decisive; the store makes the total larger still. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask whether the 5 m includes the store, and get the total external footprint before assuming exemption — add any existing shed to it.

A 5 m ROOM WITH STORAGE CONCEALED IN THE SAME ENVELOPE — and the record where the range's measurement gap is at its sharpest. The certified layer notes specifically that IT IS NOT STATED whether the hidden store sits inside the quoted 5 m, and integral storage counts toward the SAME 30 m2 combined allowance. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE and nothing has been estimated. SLIDING DOORS ALSO SUIT A UNIT WITH A STORE, since the store door and the room door need not compete for swing space. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask specifically whether the 5 m includes the store — on this configuration that single answer can decide exemption.

A LARGE CONTEMPORARY ROOM IN BLACK COMPOSITE WITH SLIDING DOORS — the most modern-looking configuration at the top end of the range, and a low-maintenance finish on a building that will be a visible object for decades. THE 6 m BAND'S PLANNING POSITION APPLIES IN FULL: a width above 5 m would exceed the 30 m2 combined allowance, no width is published, no footprint is derivable and nothing has been estimated. SLIDING DOORS SUIT A LONG BUILDING set along a boundary. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the finish and the doors are settled; the width is the open question and it decides the exemption.

A LARGE COMPOSITE ROOM WITH CONCEALED STORAGE — AND THE SIZE BAND WHERE THE ALLOWANCE STARTS TO BIND. The certified layer records both halves of the problem: at 6 m a width above 5 m exceeds the 30 m2 combined allowance, AND THE HIDDEN STORE COUNTS TOWARD THAT SAME ALLOWANCE. No width is published, no footprint is derivable, nothing has been estimated. NAVY COMPOSITE IS A DISTINCTIVE FINISH offered nowhere else in the range at this size. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the FULL external footprint in writing, store included — this is a configuration where an assumption could be expensive.

THE MOST GLAZED CONFIGURATION IN THE RANGE — a six-metre bifold front AND a picture window, which is a deliberate choice to prioritise light and view over wall and enclosure. THE PLANNING POSITION IS THE 6 m BAND'S: a width above 5 m would exceed the 30 m2 combined allowance, and no width is published, so no footprint is derivable and nothing has been estimated. FOR A GARDEN WITH A VIEW WORTH HAVING, this is the record that makes most of it. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: get the width in writing — at 6 m the exemption genuinely turns on it.

A LARGE TIMBER ROOM THAT OPENS ALONG ITS FRONT — AND THE SIZE BAND WHERE THE MISSING WIDTH BECOMES DECISION-CRITICAL. The certified layer records it plainly: at 6 m length, A WIDTH ABOVE 5 m WOULD EXCEED THE 30 m2 COMBINED ALLOWANCE, and no width is published. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE and nothing has been estimated. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THAT SIX METRES OF BIFOLD IS A GENUINELY LARGE OPENING, turning the room into a covered extension of the garden. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a room you should not order without the width in writing.

A LARGE TEAK-CLAD ROOM WITH A THREE-METRE SLIDING OPENING — AND THE RECORD WHERE A HOMEOWNER IS MOST LIKELY TO MISREAD THE NAME. THE 3 m IN THE PRODUCT NAME IS A DOOR WIDTH, NOT A BUILDING DIMENSION, and the certified layer records explicitly that it has NOT been read as one. The only building dimension published is the 6 m length; no width is given, no footprint is derivable, nothing has been estimated. AT 6 m A WIDTH ABOVE 5 m WOULD EXCEED the 30 m2 combined allowance. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not mistake the door width for the building width — ask for the external footprint.

THE LARGEST AND MOST COMPLETE BUILDING IN THE RANGE — seven metres, navy composite, concealed storage — AND THE ONE WITH THE MOST EXPOSED PLANNING POSITION. At 7 m the certified layer names this the binding size band: any width above roughly 4.3 m exceeds the 30 m2 combined allowance, AND THE HIDDEN STORE COUNTS TOWARD THE SAME ALLOWANCE. No width is published, no footprint is derivable, nothing has been estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this configuration needs the total external footprint, store included, before anything else — and on most gardens it will not be exempt.

THE RANGE'S LARGEST SIZE WITH A THREE-METRE FRENCH OPENING — AND TWO NUMBERS IN THE NAME, ONLY ONE OF WHICH IS A BUILDING DIMENSION. The certified layer records it explicitly: THE 3 m IS A DOOR WIDTH, NOT A BUILDING DIMENSION. The only building figure published is the 7 m length, and at 7 m ANY WIDTH ABOVE ROUGHLY 4.3 m EXCEEDS the 30 m2 combined allowance. No footprint is derivable; nothing has been estimated. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: obtain the external footprint in writing before ordering — and do not read 7 × 3 as the building.

SEVEN METRES OF TIMBER ROOM WITH A SINGLE DOOR AND A PICTURE WINDOW — the most enclosed configuration in the largest size band, which makes it the one with the most usable wall. THE PLANNING POSITION IS THE BAND'S AND IT IS THE TIGHTEST IN THE RANGE: at 7 m any width above roughly 4.3 m exceeds the 30 m2 combined allowance, no width is published, no footprint is derivable and nothing has been estimated. The certified layer flags this size band as the one where the missing dimension is DECISION-BLOCKING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a lot of room and a lot of wall — but the footprint must come first.

THE LARGEST SIZE BAND IN THE RANGE, AND THE ONE THE CERTIFIED LAYER NAMES AS BINDING. At 7 m length, ANY WIDTH ABOVE ROUGHLY 4.3 m PUTS THE UNIT OVER 30 m2 — and no width is published. NO FOOTPRINT IS DERIVABLE and nothing has been estimated, so the missing second dimension is MATERIALLY DECISION-BLOCKING here rather than merely inconvenient. WHAT IS SETTLED IS THAT SEVEN METRES OF TEAK-CLAD ROOM WITH FRENCH DOORS AND A WINDOW is a substantial second living space with light from two points. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not order before you have the footprint in writing.

THE LARGEST LOGHOUSE GARDEN ROOM AND THE CLOSEST TO THE LIMIT — 24.4 m2 leaving 5.6 m2 of the combined allowance. The certified record identifies it as the tightest margin in the range. UNDER THE PRE-27 JULY 2026 RULE IT SAT WITHIN 0.6 m2 OF THE OLD 25 m2 THRESHOLD, which is as close as any product in this catalogue came to the previous limit without crossing it. THE 5.2 m × 4.7 m PLAN IS NEARLY SQUARE, giving the most genuinely open floor of any model here — which is what a studio use actually needs. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the best room in the range, on the least margin.

A SELF-CONTAINED HOME FOR ONE PERSON — AND THE ONE SIZE IN THIS RANGE THAT FALLS BETWEEN BOTH IRISH EXEMPTIONS. At 25.00 m2 it is a habitable dwelling, so the 30 m2 incidental garden-structure exemption does not apply to it at all: exempted garden structures permit NO HUMAN HABITATION, whatever their size. Nor does it reach the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling route introduced by S.I. 338 of 2026, which starts at 32 m2 — this product sits 7 m2 below that floor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the smallest flat in the range is the one that needs FULL PLANNING PERMISSION, because it is too small to qualify for the new fast route and too habitable for the old one.

A HOUSEHOLD THAT NEEDS SOMEONE TO LIVE IN THE GARDEN, NOT WORK IN IT — AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT PROJECT ENTIRELY. The supplier's own designation is Studio LIVING Pod, and the certified AM-006 layer records that habitable use falls outside the Class 3 garden-structure exemption at any floor area. So this is not a garden office that happens to have a bed; it is accommodation, and it belongs in a conversation about consent, services and building standards rather than about desk space. THE ONE SIZE SIGNAL HELD is the supplier's own '25m2 +' — a starting size with an open upper end, not a figure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: right product only if you genuinely need a self-contained living space and are prepared to treat it as a dwelling proposal from day one. If you want a workspace, almost every other supplier in this catalogue is a better fit.

Best for a garden with depth rather than boundary length, where a 9 m2 room with an outdoor terrace in front of it suits the plot better than a structure running along a fence. The 318 cm width keeps the elevation narrow.

Best for a deep garden where a 512 cm width and 769 cm depth suits a plot running away from the house, and where a 25 m2 room with a substantial covered veranda is wanted. Suited to an owner prepared to address planning.

Best for a household wanting a large sheltered outdoor area in the supplier's thickest wall specification, with a small lockable room attached. The 678 cm length suits a boundary run; the enclosed 7.5 m2 suits storage or a bar rather than a working room.

Best for a household that wants the room to open fully onto the garden rather than sit behind a covered veranda, and that prefers the slightly wider of the two David models. A 19 m2 room on a 20.35 m2 footprint suits a garden where ground is limited but the outlook is good.

Best for a household that wants the room to open fully onto the garden in summer rather than to sit behind a covered veranda — the folding doors substitute for outdoor structure. A 19 m2 room on a 20.17 m2 footprint suits a garden where ground is limited but the outlook is good.

Best for a buyer wanting maximum enclosed room from a small footprint, on a site where other structures already use part of the statutory allowance. The near-square 318 x 418 cm plan suits a garden corner or the end of a modest plot.

Best for a long narrow garden with a run of nearly 9 m available, where a 22 m2 room, storage and open decking are all wanted in one line along a boundary, and where the owner is prepared to address planning.

Best for a household that needs both a garden room and outdoor storage and would rather have one structure than two. The 297 cm depth suits a boundary run of about 7 m. Suited to a site where consolidating shed and room into one footprint helps stay inside the statutory allowance.

Best for a long boundary run of nearly 9 m where a 22 m2 room, integrated storage and a covered porch are all wanted in one line, and where the owner is prepared to address planning. The 395 cm depth keeps the building close to a fence despite its length.

Best for a buyer wanting the supplier's thickest wall with a sheltered porch, at the lower end of the 70 mm price range. The 388 x 545 cm plan suits a medium garden with room at one end for the covered porch to face into.

Best for a narrow deep garden, where a 388 cm width and 669 cm depth suits a plot that runs away from the house rather than across it, and where a covered veranda facing down the garden is wanted alongside a 19 m2 room.

THE ONLY TIMBER LIVING MODEL SPECIFIED FOR AN IRISH WINTER — a 93 mm INSULATED FRAME SYSTEM with stone wool and an INTERNAL VAPOUR BARRIER, polar spruce inside and out, double-glazed window and glazed door. THE VAPOUR BARRIER IN PARTICULAR indicates a build detailed for continuous heating rather than seasonal use. ALL FOUR SIZES SIT INSIDE the 30 m2 combined allowance: 3.38m × 3.38m (11.42 m2), 4.60m × 3.38m (15.55 m2), 5.00m × 3.00m (15 m2) and 6.22m × 3.38m (21.02 m2). THE CENTIMETRE-LEVEL PRECISION suggests manufacturer dimensions rather than marketing labels. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: usable as a workspace through an Irish winter without retrofit — the only model in the range of which that can be said.

The best value building in the entire All In One Cabins range — 90m2 with 80mm walls for EUR 26,224, about EUR 291/m2. Best for a homeowner with a large site creating full independent two-bedroom accommodation who has done the arithmetic across the range.

The cheapest entry into All In One Cabins and the best value per square metre of the three Single Room models — roughly EUR 383/m2 against EUR 493 for the Kilglass and EUR 640 for the Corry. A long, low garden retreat or workspace for someone arranging their own base, electrics and assembly.

The best-balanced small cabin in the range and the cheapest route to a full one-bedroom layout. At EUR 13,389 it delivers a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, loft bed space and 70mm walls — a materially better building than the Single Room models for barely more money.

THE SMALLEST INSULATED ROOM IN THE RANGE — A SQUARE 9.00 m2 WITH NO PLANNING QUESTION. The certified layers record a 3 m × 3 m nominal designation, comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with roughly 21 m2 left over, and equally inside the pre-27 July 2026 limit. TWO THINGS MAKE IT A SENSIBLE ENTRY POINT: the plan is square, so 9 m2 works as a room rather than a corridor, and the product is explicitly sold as INSULATED, which many records at this size are not. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: a straightforward first garden office where the garden is small and the requirement is one desk.

THE LARGEST WALTONS ROOM — 24.00 m2, AND THE ONE WHERE THE 30 m2 ALLOWANCE STARTS TO BITE. A 6 m × 4 m nominal designation is genuinely a multi-purpose room: office and gym, or a studio with a seating area, rather than a single desk. IT LEAVES ROUGHLY 6 m2 OF THE COMBINED BACK-GARDEN ALLOWANCE, and that allowance is COMBINED across every garden structure — an existing shed of 8 m2 or 10 m2 would put the total over 30 m2 and remove the exemption entirely. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the right size for a room that has to do two jobs, but count what is already standing in the garden before ordering.

A children's playroom, teenage study or hobby room that needs its own bathroom — the only Single Room model in the range with one, plus a 1.5m x 2.5m decking area. Best for a homeowner who wants a self-contained small space rather than the largest possible room for the money.

A two-bedroom cabin for a homeowner who wants a better envelope than the cheaper Ree and a low profile on site. 70mm walls, German-hardware doors and the lowest ridge of any Two Bed model at 2.75m, which helps where height is constrained or overlooking is a concern.

A FIRST GARDEN ROOM AT A PUBLISHED ENTRY PRICE, FROM A SUPPLIER QUOTING IN BOTH CURRENCIES. The Ember is a compact 4.27 m x 2.44 m unit — about 10.42 m2 — published from GBP 10,000 or EUR 11,765, and the dual-currency listing with a Belfast dialling code indicates a Northern Ireland base selling into both jurisdictions. WHAT MAKES IT A SENSIBLE STARTING POINT: at roughly 10 m2 it sits comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance and was equally inside the old 25 m2 limit, so the planning question is genuinely quiet — about 20 m2 of the allowance remains for anything else in the garden. It is a single-purpose room: a desk, a chair, a bookcase. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: best for someone who wants a defined workspace and a published starting price rather than a large multi-use building.

Difficult to recommend on the evidence Atlas holds. At EUR 29,255 for 32m2 it is roughly EUR 914/m2 — more than three times the Allen's rate, and EUR 3,000 more than the Allen's 90m2 two-bedroom cabin. Only right where the site cannot take a larger footprint and a one-bedroom layout is specifically required.
A bright, roomy single-space home office, den or summerhouse on a square plot. Twelve windows across a 5m x 5m plan and a 3.6m ridge make it the most daylight-rich Single Room model in the range.

A homeowner who wants the best living space in the range rather than simply the most floor area. 100m2 with an exceptional 8.5m x 5.5m open kitchen-lounge, 80mm walls, eleven windows and outside decking — the most generous shared living area All In One Cabins offers.

THE SMALLER OF TWO GLAZED PAVILIONS — AND THE PRODUCT THAT PROVES THE DEFECT IS RANGE-WIDE. The supplier's string is preserved verbatim as '17.8m', a LINEAR METRE unit, where 17.8 linear metres is implausible for a sun room and 17.8 SQUARE METRES would be plausible. The certified layers refuse the assumption and record that the IDENTICAL ambiguity exists on the Nova 21.5m — so this is a naming convention across the Nova line, not a typo on one record. IF 17.8 m2 IS MEANT, the pavilion sits 12.2 m2 inside the allowance, comfortable headroom by the standards of this catalogue — but conditional on an unconfirmed reading. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask what the number means before doing any arithmetic with it.

A GLAZED GARDEN PAVILION — AND THE PRODUCT WHOSE OWN PUBLISHED FIGURE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. The name states '21.5m', a LINEAR METRE unit, but 21.5 linear metres is implausible for a garden pavilion while 21.5 SQUARE METRES would be plausible as an area. The certified layers record that resolving this by assuming m2 would be an INFERENCE and has NOT been made. IF THE FIGURE IS IN FACT 21.5 m2, the pavilion sits 8.5 m2 inside the allowance on its own — but that is conditional on an unconfirmed reading, and the 30 m2 is COMBINED across every structure. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not rely on the catalogue figure; ask whether 21.5 is an area or a dimension.

Maximum floor area for minimum money — 48m2 with two double bedrooms from EUR 16,176, or roughly EUR 337/m2. Best for a homeowner who needs real accommodation space on a tight budget and will upgrade the wall specification separately.

The only three-bedroom model All In One Cabins offers, and the largest at 120m2. Best for a homeowner housing a whole family independently — three bedrooms, lounge, kitchen, bathroom, storage room and separate cloakroom — at roughly EUR 304/m2.

Atlas cannot currently identify a homeowner for whom this is the right choice, and says so rather than inventing one. At EUR 53,328 for 28.14m2 it is roughly EUR 1,895/m2 — 6.5 times The Allen's rate, and EUR 16,889 MORE than the 120m2 three-bedroom Scannal. Do not buy this without asking the supplier directly what justifies the price.

HABITABLE ACCOMMODATION — AND THE AREA TEST IS NOT THE DECISIVE ONE. The certified record is explicit: an ANNEXE implies habitable accommodation, and habitable use is excluded from the Class 3 back-garden structure exemption REGARDLESS OF SIZE, so the 30 m2 allowance is not the operative test here. THE CLASS 3A DETACHED AUXILIARY DWELLING ROUTE MAY APPLY INSTEAD — habitable units of 32–45 m2 to the rear, on 14 days' notice, expiring 31 December 2030 — but whether this product qualifies has NOT been determined and is not inferred, and no area is published to test it. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: do not buy this expecting garden-office exemption.

Best for an ENGLISH buyer wanting self-contained annexe accommodation — kitchen and bathroom — built to a width of their choosing on a well-documented steel envelope, WITHOUT a concrete base. The certified thermal layer establishes the specification: 90 mm ECOTHERM floor insulation and 90 mm ACTIS in walls and ceiling, A-rated double glazing described as thermally equivalent to triple glazing, 75 mm galvanised steel-clad panels, corrugated bitumen roof, PLASTERED internal finish, FULL ELECTRICS, and a 25-YEAR STRUCTURAL GUARANTEE. The Annexe is offered straight or L-shape; this is the straight, made to width. NOT FOR AN IRISH BUYER AS A LIVE PURCHASE, on two grounds: free delivery and installation are ENGLAND only, GBP 899 to Scotland, NO IRISH ROUTE PUBLISHED, from a Corby, Northamptonshire base; and the supplier's own claim that it is 'installable under the Caravan Act with no planning permission' is a UK legal route that DOES NOT APPLY IN IRELAND. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: excellent envelope disclosure; the consent claim must be ignored on this island.

A PROPER SINGLE-PURPOSE OFFICE WITH THE RANGE'S HIGHER INSULATION SPECIFICATION. The certified layers record a 4 m × 3 m nominal designation giving 12.00 m2 — inside the 30 m2 combined allowance with about 18 m2 to spare, and inside the pre-2026 limit too. THE PREMIUM DESIGNATION IS THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE: the certified AM-001 record notes the wall build-up is thicker than a single-skin cabin of the same nominal size, which is what makes a room usable through an Irish winter. THE COROLLARY IS THAT THE INTERIOR IS SMALLER than 12 m2 by an unpublished amount. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: buy it for the envelope, and confirm the internal dimensions before planning the layout.

Homeowners who want the largest insulated room they can get for the money and are willing to accept a timber building that needs annual maintenance to keep its guarantee alive. The best floor-area-per-pound in this review set.

A COMPLETE WELLNESS SETUP IN ONE UNIT — THE ONLY COMBINED SAUNA-AND-TUB PRODUCT IN THIS CATALOGUE. For a household that wants both heat and water, buying them as one build avoids two separate installations, two bases and two sets of services. THE PLANNING CONSEQUENCE IS THE COROLLARY: the certified AM-006 layer records that the whole unit occupies one continuous footprint, and because the sauna element is an enclosed structure the buyer must count the OVERALL external footprint toward the 30 m2 allowance — not the sauna cabin alone. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most capable wellness record here, and the most demanding on garden allowance.

A SAUNA SIZED TO THE GARDEN RATHER THAN TO A CATALOGUE. The certified AM-001 layer records this as a CUSTOM-configured barrel sauna: length, and therefore floor area, are specified per order. UNLIKE THE TUBS IN THIS RANGE IT IS AN ENCLOSED STRUCTURE, so its footprint counts toward the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance in full — which makes the made-to-order length an advantage, because the building can be specified to whatever allowance remains. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: decide the length by subtracting your existing garden structures from 30 m2, not by choosing the biggest bench layout you like.

A HOT TUB BUYER, NOT A GARDEN ROOM BUYER. The certified AM-001 layer classifies this NOT A FLOOR-AREA PRODUCT: a wood-fired tub is a vessel, not an enclosed structure, and the published '4-8 person' figure is a bathing capacity, not an area. It sits under Garden Rooms only because Atlas has no correct category. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge it as wellness equipment — heater type, capacity, timber, water management — and ignore any comparison with garden offices, which measure a different thing entirely.

A COMPACT NAMED MODEL WITH TWO UNDEFINED MODIFIERS ON IT. 'Tonio' carries no recorded form or specification; the numeral is a nominal name rather than a size, as the certified layers state for every Bertilo product; and 'PLUS' is a third designation with nothing recorded against it at all — it may denote extra size, extra specification or extra equipment, and none of those has been inferred. NO AUDITED AREA, HEIGHT OR ROOF FORM IS HELD, so no statutory test can be run. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: three words, none of them measurable — ask what 'Plus' adds before anything else.

THE SECOND TONIO — AND, LIKE THE FIRST, A NAME PLUS A NUMERAL PLUS A SUFFIX, NONE OF THEM MEASURABLE. The certified layers record that Bertilo numerals are nominal names rather than square metres, so the step from Tonio 1 Plus is not quantified; and 'Plus' has no recorded content on either model. EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY BETWEEN THE TWO IS PRESERVED DELIBERATELY. NO AUDITED AREA, HEIGHT OR ROOF FORM IS HELD, so neither the 30 m2 allowance nor the height limits can be tested. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you are comparing the two Tonios, only the supplier can tell you what differs.

THE SAME ANSWER AS ITS SISTER MODEL, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING. Atlas holds no floor area, no dimensions, no height, no specification, no warranty and no price for The Lagan, and the model name carries no size information — so nothing distinguishes it from The Sperrin in the record, and neither can be matched to a requirement. A buyer cannot tell from Atlas which of the two models is larger, warmer, cheaper or better suited to their garden. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the choice between these two models cannot be made from published information at all. It has to be made in person at the Belfast show village, or from a written specification requested from the supplier — and the first question is simply how the two models differ.

A NORTHERN IRELAND BUYER FIRST — AND EVEN THERE, ONLY AFTER THE BASIC NUMBERS ARE ASKED FOR. Total Garden Rooms operates from a show village in Belfast (2 Advantage Way, BT13 3LZ), which is a real advantage in itself: a buyer can walk into a building before ordering one, and very few suppliers in this catalogue offer that. WHAT ATLAS CANNOT TELL YOU: no floor area, no dimensions, no height, no specification, no warranty and no price is held for The Sperrin, and the model name carries no size information. The certified AM-006 layer records that neither the area nor the height test could be run. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a supplier best approached in person, where the missing figures can be measured and asked for directly — not one to shortlist from a screen.

A HOUSE, NOT A GARDEN ROOM — AND THE CERTIFIED LAYERS SAY SO IN THOSE TERMS. Published dimensions of 7.94 m × 6.08 m give 48.28 m2: more than 18 m2 over the 30 m2 combined allowance, AND above the 45 m2 ceiling of the Class 3A Detached Auxiliary Dwelling band, so no exemption route reaches it on area. ON USE IT FAILS INDEPENDENTLY: the supplier's own designation is TWO BEDROOM and RESIDENTIAL, which is habitable accommodation, and the Class 3 exemption excludes human habitation at any size. FULL PLANNING PERMISSION IS INDICATED. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: approach this with a designer and your local authority planning office from the outset.

Best for a large garden where two separate enclosed spaces are needed and the owner is prepared to go through planning. The 822 x 558 cm envelope requires an open area of garden rather than a boundary strip.

Best for a household needing two separate spaces rather than one — a study alongside a hobby room, or a workshop with a clean room — in the supplier's thickest wall specification, on a garden with no other outbuildings.

NO HOMEOWNER — THIS RECORD SHOULD NOT BE SURFACED IN ITS PRESENT STATE. The certified AM-001 layer is unusually direct about it: no area, no dimensions, no product URL, a name that describes a RANGE rather than a building, and — at the time of that layer's certification — no organisation link at all, making it the only Garden Room record in Atlas with no supplier attached. Its own conclusion was that the record cannot be measured, priced, planning-assessed or attributed, and should not reach homeowners. NOTHING IN THIS LAYER CHANGES THAT. 'Ultimate' is a marketing superlative, not a specification, and it has not been read as one. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if you have encountered this range elsewhere, establish first which company actually makes it, then ask for model names and external dimensions.

Homeowners who want thermal performance expressed as numbers rather than adjectives, and who accept manufacturer-declared figures. This is one of very few garden rooms in Atlas that publishes any U-value set at all — approximate, self-declared, but quantified — and it arrives with electrics fitted and itemised, a steel foundation system included, and delivery, installation and VAT in the price. Best suited to a UK buyer: Sanctum publishes no Irish purchasing route.

UK homeowners who never want to paint, stain or treat a garden building again. The Urban range is composite clad and the supplier states the cladding holds its colour year after year with no repainting or staining. Best for a small garden where the building will be highly visible and expected to look new in ten years.

A LARGER FAMILY CABIN — AND THE USE QUESTION MAY SETTLE ITS PLANNING POSITION BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT DOES. The certified record makes the point directly: a cabin the supplier itself describes as FAMILY accommodation implies habitable use, and the Class 3 exemption requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house and EXCLUDES HUMAN HABITATION AT ANY SIZE. If it is intended as living or sleeping accommodation it falls outside Class 3 however small it is. 'XL' AND 'FAMILY' ARE MARKETING LABELS, NOT MEASUREMENTS, and have not been treated as such — no area, dimension or height is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: decide what the building is for first; the tape measure comes second.

NOT CURRENTLY RECOMMENDABLE TO AN IRISH HOMEOWNER — EVIDENCE UNAVAILABLE. Atlas holds no size, no specification, no price and no Irish purchasing route for the Vilarte Pavilion, and the only URL held is a concept page rather than a product page. There is therefore no basis on which to say who this product suits, and none has been invented. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this record cannot support a buying decision as it stands. If the design appeals, treat it as a starting point for a direct enquiry to Vilarte rather than as a comparable product — and establish first whether the company sells and installs into Ireland at all, because Atlas holds no evidence that it does.

A LONG, SHALLOW ROOM THAT LEAVES HALF THE ALLOWANCE FREE — 15 m2 on Quick-Garden's verified external footprint against the 30 m2 combined back-garden limit. IT IS THE ONLY WISSOUS MODEL IN ATLAS, and on published evidence it is indistinguishable from the PREMIUM 5 × 3 m at the same footprint: EVIDENCE NEUTRALITY BETWEEN THEM IS PRESERVED. A 3 m DEPTH ALONG A BOUNDARY takes very little garden and reads as a wall rather than a building. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: an easy planning position; the depth and the unstated wall class are what to test.

A GENERAL-PURPOSE HOME WORKSHOP AT THE ENTRY POINT OF THE LINE — no craft designation, so no assumption about what happens inside beyond the general one. THE USE CONDITION STILL GOVERNS: the certified record warns that a workshop used for a trade or business may fall outside the exemption entirely, since Class 3 requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house. THE NUMERAL IS A NOMINAL NAME, NOT A SIZE, and no audited area or height is held, so neither statutory test can be run. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the simplest workshop record in the range, with the same use question attached.

THE MIDDLE OF A THREE-MODEL WORKSHOP LINE — for a household whose making and storage has outgrown the smallest option. THE CERTIFIED RECORD REPEATS THE USE CAUTION IN ITS FULLEST FORM: a workshop used for a trade or business RATHER THAN DOMESTIC PURPOSES may fall outside the exemption entirely, because Class 3 requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house. THE NUMERAL IS A NOMINAL NAME, NOT A SIZE, and no audited area or height is held, so neither statutory test can be run. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the use question first, the footprint second.

THE LARGEST-NAMED WORKSHOP IN THE RANGE — AND THE ONE WHERE BOTH BERTILO CAUTIONS BITE HARDEST. The certified record warns that a workshop used for a trade or business may fall outside the exemption entirely; and the numeral, as throughout the range, is a nominal name rather than a size, so it is not established that this is larger than the Workshop 1 or 2. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, so neither the 30 m2 combined allowance nor the height limits can be tested. ESTONIA-ONLY SHIPPING, NO IRISH DISTRIBUTOR. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the biggest workshop in an unmeasured line, with the use question fully live.

A HOME WORKSHOP — AND THE ONE BERTILO CATEGORY WHERE INTENDED USE MATTERS AS MUCH AS SIZE. The certified record states it directly: a workshop used for a TRADE OR BUSINESS rather than domestic purposes may fall outside the exemption ENTIRELY, because the Class 3 exemption requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house. A HOBBYIST'S WORKSHOP IS INCIDENTAL; A JOINERY BUSINESS IS NOT, and the model name points squarely at woodworking. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD, and shipping is Estonia-only with no Irish distributor. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: be honest about whether the work is paid — that answer decides the planning route.

A METALWORKING OR HEAVIER-CRAFT WORKSHOP, ON THE SUPPLIER'S OWN NAMING — and the same use condition governs it. The certified record repeats the caution: a workshop used for a trade or business may fall outside the exemption entirely, since Class 3 requires use incidental to the enjoyment of the house. A SMITHY RAISES A FURTHER PRACTICAL POINT the catalogue does not address: heat, sparks and ventilation are not garden-room considerations, and no specification of any kind is published. NO AUDITED AREA OR HEIGHT IS HELD; Estonia-only shipping. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: intended use matters as much as size, and here so does what you will be doing inside.

NO BUYER CAN BE MATCHED TO THIS PRODUCT FROM THE EVIDENCE HELD, and saying otherwise would be an invention. The certified thermal layer classifies it REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION and records the conclusion directly: 'an unclassified record; NOT USABLE IN A COMPARISON until a specification is obtained from the supplier.' No construction specification, insulation material, thickness or U-value is held. The certified measurement layer holds NO AREA, NO DIMENSIONS and no derivable footprint. The model name is branding with no dimensional content. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, and it is only three things: a TURNKEY INSTALLATION scope published as running from initial design consultations to final installation with no self-assembly route; a COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY published as LIFETIME; and availability recorded as AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND, though coverage could not be verified. THE CAUSE: x-genhomes.com is client-rendered, returns an empty body to direct fetch, and is on the Atlas permanently-unreadable list. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is a supplier enquiry, not a product comparison. Contact them directly.

BEST FOR A BUYER WILLING TO DO THE SUPPLIER'S DISCLOSURE WORK THEMSELVES — and that is the honest position the certified evidence supports. The certified thermal layer classifies this product REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION: no construction specification, no insulation material, no thickness and no U-value could be obtained, and the certified measurement layer holds NO AREA, NO DIMENSIONS and no derivable footprint. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: a TURNKEY INSTALLATION scope published as running from initial design consultations to final installation, with no self-assembly route; a COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY published as LIFETIME; and a HEXAGONAL PLAN, which is the one genuinely distinctive thing about the product — a shape no other supplier in this Atlas offers, and a striking one in a garden. THE RETRIEVAL BARRIER BEHIND ALL OF THIS: x-genhomes.com is client-rendered, returns an empty body to direct fetch, and is on the Atlas permanently-unreadable list. Every value held rests on indexed evidence. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the hexagonal form is what you want, contact the supplier directly — nothing readable is published.

BEST FOR A BUYER MAKING A DIRECT ENQUIRY, NOT A COMPARISON — the certified evidence supports nothing stronger. The certified thermal layer classifies this REQUIRES PRODUCT-SPECIFIC VERIFICATION: no construction specification, insulation material, thickness or U-value could be obtained. The certified measurement layer holds NO AREA and records that the 'MICRO' DESIGNATION IS NOT A MEASUREMENT and has not been treated as one — it indicates a small unit and nothing more. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: a TURNKEY INSTALLATION scope published as running from initial design consultations to final installation, with no self-assembly route; a COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT WARRANTY published as LIFETIME; availability recorded as AVAILABLE IN REPUBLIC OF IRELAND with coverage unverifiable. THE CERTIFIED THERMAL LAYER ADDS A POINT THAT MATTERS PARTICULARLY HERE: at micro-office scale the envelope matters PROPORTIONALLY MORE than on a large building, because external surface area is high relative to floor — so the missing specification is MORE consequential on this product than its small size might suggest. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: ask for the footprint and the wall build-up before anything else.

A LARGE MULTI-USE ROOM FOR A BUYER WITH AN OTHERWISE EMPTY GARDEN. Published as a 6.2 m × 4.2 m FOOTPRINT of 26.04 m2 with 24 m2 of LIVING SPACE and a 2.5-3 m height. At 24 m2 usable and 4 m of internal depth this is a genuine two-zone room — office and gym, or studio and storage — rather than a large corridor. THE PLANNING POSITION IS THE CRITICAL PART AND THE CERTIFIED LAYER IS EXPLICIT: on the FOOTPRINT, which is what the regulation measures, 26.04 m2 exceeded the 25 m2 limit that applied before 27 July 2026, so this product is exempt only because of the 2026 increase, with under 4 m2 of the combined allowance left over. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the most room you can take from this supplier without a planning application — provided nothing else stands in the garden.

THE MIDDLE YARDBOX, AND THE ONE MOST HOMEOWNERS ACTUALLY NEED. Published as a 5.2 m × 3.2 m FOOTPRINT of 16.64 m2, with 15 m2 of LIVING SPACE stated separately and a 2.5 m HEIGHT — all three figures from the supplier's own comparison table. The certified layers place it inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance and inside the 3 m height limit for a non-pitched roof, so both statutory tests pass on published evidence rather than assumption. 15 m2 USABLE IS THE THRESHOLD AT WHICH A ROOM STOPS BEING A POD: desk plus meeting chairs, or office plus exercise space, with 3 m of clear depth to make the second function workable. AND IT IS OBTAINABLE — Co. Down based, serving Ireland and Northern Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the strongest all-round mid-size record in this catalogue on evidence quality.

A COMPACT OFFICE FOR A BUYER WHO WANTS TO KNOW EXACTLY WHAT THEY ARE GETTING. The Whistler is the clearest small record in this Atlas: Yardbox publishes a 3.2 m × 3.2 m FOOTPRINT of 10.24 m2, 9 m2 of LIVING SPACE separately, and a 2.5 m HEIGHT — three figures where most suppliers publish none. The certified layers could therefore test both statutory criteria: comfortably inside the 30 m2 combined back-garden allowance with about 20 m2 to spare, and inside the 3 m height limit for a non-pitched roof. THE SQUARE PLAN IS THE PRACTICAL ADVANTAGE at this size: 3 m clear internally in both directions is a usable room, where the same area in a long shallow plan is a corridor. AND IT IS OBTAINABLE: Co. Down based, stating service to Ireland and Northern Ireland. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the small-room benchmark in this catalogue.

A LONGER VERSION OF A MIRROR-GLASS UNIT THAT WAS NEVER DESIGNED FOR AN IRISH BACK GARDEN. ÖÖD builds modular mirror-clad buildings marketed for glamping and hospitality, and the Extended House is the stretched variant of the base model. THE NAME IS THE ONLY SIZE SIGNAL AND IT IS NOT A MEASUREMENT: the certified layers record 'Extended' as a marketing term that has NOT been read as a figure, and no floor area, dimension or product URL is published. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: if the appeal is the mirrored aesthetic, this is the larger of the two standard forms — but nothing about its size, height or Irish availability can be confirmed from published evidence.

COMMERCIAL GLAMPING ACCOMMODATION — NOT A GARDEN ROOM, AND THE PRODUCT NAME SAYS SO. The certified AM-006 record is unambiguous: the intended use is glamping accommodation, which is commercial hospitality and overnight habitation, and NEITHER is use incidental to the enjoyment of a house. This product therefore falls OUTSIDE the Class 3 garden-structure exemption ON USE ALONE, at any floor area. Commercial letting in a domestic back garden is additionally a CHANGE OF USE normally requiring planning permission in its own right, independently of the size of the building. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: the planning question here is about change of use, not about 30 m2, and it belongs with your local authority before any purchase.

THE MOST HEAVILY GLAZED UNIT IN THE RANGE — AND THE ONE WHOSE MAIN OBSTACLE IS NOT A REGULATION AT ALL. The certified AM-006 record makes the point directly: a heavily glazed unit sited in a back garden raises OVERLOOKING AND PRIVACY questions with neighbours that sit OUTSIDE the exemption tests entirely. A building can pass 30 m2 and 3 m and still generate a complaint, an objection or an enforcement query. FOR A SECLUDED OR RURAL SITE that concern largely disappears and the glazing becomes the whole point. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: judge this product on the site as much as on the specification — and neither its area nor its height is published.

A RELOCATABLE MIRROR-GLASS UNIT — AND THE PRODUCT THAT MAY NOT BE GOVERNED BY THE GARDEN-STRUCTURE RULES AT ALL. The certified AM-006 record raises a question the area test never reaches: a MOBILE unit may fall outside fixed-structure exempted development entirely, in which case Class 3 is not the applicable test and a different set of controls applies. THAT QUESTION WAS NOT DECIDED, because Atlas evidence cannot resolve it. FOR A BUYER WHO GENUINELY NEEDS TO MOVE THE BUILDING — a rented site, a phased development, a temporary use — relocatability is a real capability. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: mobility changes which rules apply, not whether any apply.

A COMPACT MIRROR-GLASS UNIT — AND THE ONE WHERE THE CERTIFIED LAYERS FLAG HEIGHT RATHER THAN AREA AS THE LIKELY CONSTRAINT. The AM-006 record for this product notes that mirror-glass units are typically TALL FOR THEIR FOOTPRINT, so the 3 m flat-roof limit may bind before the 30 m2 area limit does. No floor area, dimension, height or product URL is published, so neither test can actually be run. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: with this product, ask for the OVERALL HEIGHT ABOVE FINISHED GROUND LEVEL — not the internal ceiling height, which is the figure suppliers more readily give and the one the regulation does not measure.

THE RANGE'S FLAGSHIP FORM — AND THE ONE PRODUCT HERE WITH A NAME PROBLEM WORTH KNOWING ABOUT. The certified AM-001 layer records a NAMING CAUTION: 'Signature' is also used as a range name by Luxury Garden Studios elsewhere in Atlas, the two are unrelated, they must not be matched on name, and NO DIMENSION HAS BEEN CARRIED ACROSS between them. A homeowner researching 'ÖÖD Signature' online can easily land on another supplier's specification and believe it applies. NO AREA, DIMENSION, HEIGHT OR PRODUCT URL is published for this product. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: when comparing figures, confirm you are reading ÖÖD's own material and not a similarly named product from a different company.

THE LARGEST-SOUNDING UNIT IN THE RANGE — AND THE ONE WHERE THE MISSING FIGURES MATTER MOST. The certified AM-001 layer records explicitly that 'Big' is a MARKETING LABEL, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and it has not been treated as one: no floor area, dimension or product URL is published for this product any more than for the others. THE LOGIC RECORDED IN THE CERTIFIED PLANNING LAYER IS THE POINT — the larger the building, the closer it sits to the 30 m2 threshold, and the less a homeowner can afford to guess. HOMEOWNER IMPLICATION: this is the ÖÖD product on which you should least accept a verbal answer about size.
